title.zh: 卷二百十三 列傳第一百〇一 徐階 高拱 張居正
title.en: Volume 213 Biographies 101: Xu Jie, Gao Gong, Zhang Juzheng
title.raw: 卷二百十三 列傳第一百〇一 徐階 高拱 張居正 Volume 213 Biographies 101: Xu Jie, Gao Gong, Zhang Juzheng

sentences.zh: 徐階弟:陟 子:璠 等 高拱附:郭樸 張居正曾孫:同敞

translations.literal: Xu Jie's younger brother: Sheng; sons: Fan and others. Appended to Gao Gong: Guo Pu. Zhang Juzheng's great-grandson: Tongchang.
translations.idiomatic: Related figures: Xu Jie's younger brother Sheng and his sons including Fan; with Gao Gong's account, Guo Pu is included; Zhang Juzheng's great-grandson was Tongchang.

sentences.zh: 徐階，字子升，松江華亭人。

translations.literal: Xu Jie, style Zisheng, was a native of Huating in Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jie, whose style was Zisheng, came from Huating in Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 生甫周歲，墮眢井，出三日而蘇。

translations.literal: When he had just completed one year of life, he fell into a dry well and revived after three days.
translations.idiomatic: Barely a year old, he fell into an abandoned well and did not come to until three days later.

sentences.zh: 五歲從父道括蒼，墮高嶺，衣掛於樹不死。

translations.literal: At five he followed his father on the road to Kuocang, fell from a high ridge, and his clothes caught on a tree so that he did not die.
translations.idiomatic: At five, traveling with his father toward Kuocang, he tumbled from a high cliff; his garment snagged on a tree and saved his life.

sentences.zh: 人咸異之。

translations.literal: Everyone regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: People everywhere marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年進士第三人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing he placed third among the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1523 he took third place on the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 授翰林院編修，予歸娶。

translations.literal: He was appointed Compiler in the Hanlin Academy and granted leave to return home to marry.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a Hanlin compiler and sent home on leave to marry.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服除，補故官。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his father; when the mourning ended he resumed his former post.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he observed mourning, then returned to his former office.

sentences.zh: 階為人短小白皙，善容止。

translations.literal: Jie was short in stature, fair-skinned, and graceful in bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was slight and fair-complexioned, with an easy, polished manner.

sentences.zh: 性穎敏，有權略，而陰重不泄。

translations.literal: By nature he was keen and clever, possessed of stratagem, yet inwardly guarded and never revealing himself.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and resourceful, he was inwardly reserved and never let his designs show.

sentences.zh: 讀書為古文辭，從王守仁門人游，有聲士大夫間。

translations.literal: He studied and wrote ancient-style prose, associated with disciples of Wang Shouren, and gained a reputation among scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely and wrote in the classical style, moved among Wang Yangming's followers, and won esteem among the literati.

sentences.zh: 帝用張孚敬議，欲去孔子王號，易像為木主，籩豆禮樂皆有所損抑。

translations.literal: The emperor adopted Zhang Fuyi's proposal to remove Confucius's title of king, replace his image with a wooden tablet, and reduce the vessels, music, and ritual in various ways.
translations.idiomatic: Following Zhang Fuyi's advice, the emperor sought to strip Confucius of his royal title, replace his statue with a spirit tablet, and pare back the ritual vessels, music, and ceremony.

sentences.zh: 下儒臣議，階獨持不可。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Confucian officials for discussion; Jie alone maintained that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When the court asked the Confucian officials to deliberate, Jie alone stood firm against the change.

sentences.zh: 孚敬召階盛氣詰之，階抗辯不屈。

translations.literal: Fuyi summoned Jie and questioned him in a towering rage; Jie argued back and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyi summoned him and berated him hotly, but Jie argued back without bending.

sentences.zh: 孚敬怒曰：「若叛我。」

translations.literal: Fuyi said angrily, "You have betrayed me.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyi snapped, "So you have turned against me.

sentences.zh: 階正色曰：「叛生於附。

translations.literal: Jie said with a stern countenance, "Betrayal arises from having first attached oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Jie answered gravely, "One can betray only after one has first attached oneself.

sentences.zh: 階未嘗附公，何得言叛？」

translations.literal: I have never attached myself to you, sir—how can you speak of betrayal?"
translations.idiomatic: I never attached myself to you, sir—how can you call this betrayal?"

sentences.zh: 長揖出。

translations.literal: He made a long bow and left.
translations.idiomatic: With a deep bow he walked out.

sentences.zh: 斥為延平府推官。

translations.literal: He was demoted to Judicial Assessor of Yanping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was banished to serve as judicial assessor in Yanping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 連攝郡事。

translations.literal: He successively acted as prefect in charge of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly called on to administer the prefecture in the magistrate's stead.

sentences.zh: 出繫囚三百，毀淫祠，創鄉社學，捕劇盜百二十人。

translations.literal: He released three hundred prisoners held in custody, destroyed illicit shrines, founded village community schools, and arrested one hundred twenty notorious bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He freed three hundred prisoners, tore down illicit shrines, founded village schools, and seized a hundred and twenty hardened bandits.

sentences.zh: 遷黃州府同知，擢浙江按察僉事，進江西按察副使，俱視學政。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Prefect of Huangzhou Prefecture, promoted to Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Zhejiang, and advanced to Surveillance Assistant Commissioner of Jiangxi, in each case overseeing educational administration.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from vice prefect of Huangzhou to surveillance commissioner in Zhejiang and then assistant surveillance commissioner in Jiangxi, always with charge of education.

sentences.zh: 皇太子出閣，召拜司經局洗馬兼翰林院侍講。

translations.literal: When the crown prince left the palace school, Jie was summoned and appointed Reader in the Directorate of the Classics and Concurrent Lecturer in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince left the inner quarters, Jie was summoned as reader in the Classics Directorate and Hanlin lecturer.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂歸。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 服除，擢國子祭酒，遷禮部右侍郎，尋改吏部。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was promoted to Chancellor of the National University, transferred to Right Vice Minister of Rites, and soon moved to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he became chancellor of the National University, then right vice minister of Rites, and soon after moved to Personnel.

sentences.zh: 故事，吏部率鐍門，所接見庶官不數語。

translations.literal: By precedent the Ministry of Personnel habitually kept its gates barred and exchanged only a few words with the lower officials it received.
translations.idiomatic: By custom the Ministry of Personnel kept its doors shut tight and barely spoke to the junior officials who came to call.

sentences.zh: 階折節下之。

translations.literal: Jie humbled himself to meet them on their level.
translations.idiomatic: Jie lowered himself to treat them with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 見必深坐，咨邊腹要害，吏治民瘼。

translations.literal: Whenever he received someone he would sit with him at length, inquiring about frontier vulnerabilities and interior strongpoints, official administration, and the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: He would sit with each visitor at length, asking about frontier weak points and interior defenses, bureaucratic performance, and the people's grievances.

sentences.zh: 皆自喜得階意，願為用。

translations.literal: All were pleased to have won Jie's regard and wished to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: They were all glad to have gained his confidence and eager to serve his purposes.

sentences.zh: 尚書熊浹、唐龍、周用皆重階。

translations.literal: The ministers Xiong Xian, Tang Long, and Zhou Yong all valued Jie highly.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers Xiong Xian, Tang Long, and Zhou Yong all held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 階數署部事，所引用宋景、張岳、王道、歐陽德、范皆長者。

translations.literal: Jie repeatedly acted in charge of ministry affairs; those he recommended—Song Jing, Zhang Yue, Wang Dao, Ouyang De, and Fan Yong—were all men of stature.
translations.idiomatic: Often acting head of the ministry, he promoted such seasoned men as Song Jing, Zhang Yue, Wang Dao, Ouyang De, and Fan Yong.

sentences.zh: 用卒，聞淵代，自處前輩，取立斷。

translations.literal: When Zhou Yong died, Wen Yuan succeeded him; he treated himself as Jie's senior and favored swift, decisive action.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou Yong died, Wen Yuan took his place, assumed the air of a senior, and liked to decide matters on the spot.

sentences.zh: 階意不樂，求出避之。

translations.literal: Jie was displeased and sought a transfer to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was unhappy and asked to leave the ministry to get away from him.

sentences.zh: 命兼翰林院學士，教習庶吉士。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve concurrently as Hanlin Academician and instruct the Hanlin probationers.
translations.idiomatic: He was given concurrent appointment as Hanlin academician to tutor the probationary scholars.

sentences.zh: 尋掌院事，進禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he took charge of Hanlin affairs and was promoted to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he headed the Hanlin Academy and rose to minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 帝察階勤，又所撰青詞獨稱旨，召直無逸殿。

translations.literal: The emperor observed Jie's diligence, and the green prayers he composed alone pleased the throne; he was summoned to attend at the Hall of Unceasing Vigil.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noted his diligence and was especially pleased with the Daoist prayers he drafted; Jie was called to duty in the Hall of Unceasing Vigil.

sentences.zh: 與大學士張治、李本俱賜飛魚服及上方珍饌、上尊無虛日。

translations.literal: Together with Grand Secretaries Zhang Zhi and Li Ben he was granted flying-fish robes and imperial delicacies and fine wine—not a day passed without such gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He and Grand Secretaries Zhang Zhi and Li Ben were given flying-fish robes and daily gifts of imperial delicacies and fine wine from the palace kitchens.

sentences.zh: 廷推吏部尚書，不聽，不欲階去左右也。

translations.literal: The court recommended him for Minister of Personnel, but the emperor did not approve, unwilling to let Jie leave his side.
translations.idiomatic: When the court nominated him for minister of Personnel, the emperor refused—he did not want Jie away from him.

sentences.zh: 階遂請立皇太子，不報。

translations.literal: Jie then petitioned to establish the crown prince; there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Jie then urged that a crown prince be named, but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 復連請之，皆不報。

translations.literal: He petitioned again and again; still there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the matter repeatedly, always without response.

sentences.zh: 後當冠婚，復請先裕王，後景王，帝不懌。

translations.literal: Later, when the time came for capping and marriage, he again asked that Prince Yu be placed before Prince Jing; the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When the princes came of age for capping and marriage, he again asked that Prince Yu precede Prince Jing, which displeased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 尋以推恩加太子太保。

translations.literal: Before long, as a grace extension, he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he received the additional title of grand guardian of the heir apparent as an act of grace.

sentences.zh: 俺答犯京，階請釋周尚文及戴綸、歐陽安等自效，報可。

translations.literal: When Altan attacked the capital region, Jie asked that Zhou Shangwen and Dai Lun, Ouyang An, and others be released to offer their service; the reply was approval.
translations.idiomatic: When Altan threatened the capital, Jie urged the release of Zhou Shangwen, Dai Lun, Ouyang An, and others to serve again; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 已，請帝還大內，召群臣計兵事，從之。

translations.literal: Afterward he asked the emperor to return to the inner palace and summon the officials to plan military affairs; the emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: He then urged the emperor back into the Forbidden City and to convene the court on military affairs; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 中官陷寇歸，以俺答求貢書進。

translations.literal: A eunuch who had fallen into the enemy's hands returned, presenting Altan's letter requesting tribute.
translations.idiomatic: A eunuch captured by the enemy came back bearing Altan's letter asking for tributary relations.

sentences.zh: 帝以示嚴嵩及階，召對便殿。

translations.literal: The emperor showed it to Yan Song and Xu Jie and summoned them for audience in the side hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed the letter to Yan Song and Xu Jie and called them to audience in a side hall.

sentences.zh: 嵩曰：「飢賊耳，不足患。」

translations.literal: Song said, "They are only starving bandits—nothing to worry about.
translations.idiomatic: Song said, "They are only hungry raiders—hardly worth worrying over.

sentences.zh: 階曰：「傅城而軍，殺人若刈菅，何謂飢賊？」

translations.literal: Jie said, "They camp against the walls and slaughter people like cutting reeds—how can you call them starving bandits?"
translations.idiomatic: Jie replied, "They lay siege to our cities and kill as if mowing grass—how can you call them hungry raiders?"

sentences.zh: 帝然之，問求貢書安在。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed and asked where the tribute petition was.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and asked where the tribute letter was.

sentences.zh: 嵩出諸袖曰：「禮部事也。」

translations.literal: Song produced it from his sleeve and said, "This is a matter for the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Song pulled it from his sleeve and said, "That belongs to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 帝復問階。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Jie again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Jie again.

sentences.zh: 階曰：「寇深矣，不許恐激之怒，許則彼厚要我。

translations.literal: Jie said, "The enemy is deep in our territory; if we refuse we may provoke their rage, but if we agree they will press us hard for terms.
translations.idiomatic: Jie said, "The invaders are deep inside our borders. Refusal may enrage them, but acceptance will let them drive a hard bargain.

sentences.zh: 請遣譯者紿緩之，我得益為備。

translations.literal: Please send an interpreter to deceive and delay them, so that we may better prepare our defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Send an interpreter to stall them with promises while we strengthen our defenses.

sentences.zh: 援兵集，寇且走。」

translations.literal: When relief troops gather, the enemy will soon withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Once reinforcements arrive, the raiders will withdraw.

sentences.zh: 帝稱善者再。

translations.literal: The emperor praised the plan twice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the advice twice over.

sentences.zh: 嵩、階因請帝出視朝。

translations.literal: Song and Jie therefore asked the emperor to come out and hold court.
translations.idiomatic: Song and Jie then urged the emperor to appear at court.

sentences.zh: 寇尋飽去，乃下階疏，弗許貢。

translations.literal: The enemy soon withdrew sated; only then did Jie submit a memorial refusing tribute.
translations.idiomatic: When the raiders had their fill and left, Jie submitted a memorial refusing tribute.

sentences.zh: 嵩怙寵弄權，猜害同列。

translations.literal: Song relied on favor to manipulate power and suspected and harmed his colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: Song abused the emperor's favor to wield power and systematically undermined his peers.

sentences.zh: 既仇夏言置之死，而言嘗薦階，嵩以是忌之。

translations.literal: Having already hated Xia Yan to death—and Yan had once recommended Jie—Song therefore resented Jie.
translations.idiomatic: He had already destroyed Xia Yan, who had once recommended Jie; for that reason Song came to resent Jie.

sentences.zh: 初，孝烈皇后崩，帝欲祔之廟，念壓於先孝潔皇后，又睿宗入廟非公議，恐後世議祧，遂欲當己世預祧仁宗，以孝烈先祔廟，自為一世，下禮部議。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Empress Xiaolie died, the emperor wished to enshrine her in the ancestral temple. Reflecting that she would rank below the former Empress Xiaojie, and that Emperor Ruizong's entry into the temple had not been by public consensus, he feared later generations would debate removing an ancestor. He therefore wished in his own reign to remove Emperor Renzong from the temple in advance, install Xiaolie first, and make her a separate generation, and referred the matter to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Xiaolie died, the emperor wanted her enshrined in the ancestral temple. She would rank below the late Empress Xiaojie, and Ruizong's admission had never won broad approval—he feared future debate over removing an ancestor. He therefore planned to remove Renzong from the temple in his own lifetime, install Xiaolie first as a separate generation, and sent the question to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 階抗言女後無先入廟者，請祀之奉先殿。

translations.literal: Jie argued forcefully that no empress consort had ever entered the temple before her predecessors and asked that she be worshipped in the Hall of Ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Jie argued that no empress had ever entered the main temple ahead of her predecessors and urged worship for her in the Hall of Ancestors instead.

sentences.zh: 禮科都給事中楊思忠亦以為然。

translations.literal: Yang Sizhong, supervising secretary of the Rites section, also agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sizhong, chief supervising secretary for rites, agreed with him.

sentences.zh: 疏上，帝大怒。

translations.literal: When the memorial went up, the emperor was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached him, the emperor flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 階皇恐謝罪，不能守前議。

translations.literal: Jie was terrified and begged forgiveness, unable to hold to his earlier position.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was terrified and apologized, unable to stand by his earlier view.

sentences.zh: 帝又使階往邯鄲落成呂仙祠。

translations.literal: The emperor also sent Jie to Handan to complete the shrine to the Immortal Lü.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ordered him to Handan to dedicate the shrine to the Immortal Lü.

sentences.zh: 階不欲行，乃以議祔廟解，得緩期。

translations.literal: Jie did not wish to go and used the debate over enshrinement as an excuse, gaining a postponement.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to go, he used the temple dispute as a pretext and won a delay.

sentences.zh: 至寇逼城，帝益懈，乃使尚書顧可學行，而內銜階。

translations.literal: When the enemy pressed the city, the emperor grew more lax and sent Minister Gu Kexue instead, while nursing resentment against Jie inwardly.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy reached the walls the emperor relented and sent Minister Gu Kexue in his place, but inwardly he bore a grudge against Jie.

sentences.zh: 摘思忠元旦賀表誤，廷杖之百，斥為民，以怵階。

translations.literal: He seized on an error in Sizhong's New Year's congratulatory memorial, had him beaten a hundred strokes at court, and dismissed him to commoner status, to intimidate Jie.
translations.idiomatic: He seized on a mistake in Sizhong's New Year memorial, had him beaten a hundred strokes at court, and banished him to common status to frighten Jie.

sentences.zh: 嵩因謂階可間也，中傷之百方。

translations.literal: Song therefore said Jie could be set against and slandered him in every way.
translations.idiomatic: Song decided Jie was vulnerable and attacked him from every angle.

sentences.zh: 一日獨召對，語及階，嵩徐曰：「階所乏非才，但多二心耳。」

translations.literal: One day the emperor summoned Song alone for audience; when the talk turned to Jie, Song said slowly, "What Jie lacks is not talent, but he has too divided a heart.
translations.idiomatic: One day, in a private audience, talk turned to Jie. Song said slowly, "Jie is not short of talent—only of single-minded loyalty.

sentences.zh: 蓋以其嘗請立太子也。

translations.literal: This was because Jie had once asked to establish the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He meant Jie's earlier petitions to name the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 階危甚，度未可與爭，乃謹事嵩，而益精治齋詞迎帝意，左右亦多為地者。

translations.literal: Jie was in grave danger; judging that he could not yet contend, he served Song scrupulously while refining his fasting prayers to please the emperor; those around the throne also made room for him in many ways.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was in grave peril. Seeing he could not yet fight back, he deferred to Song while polishing the ritual prayers that pleased the emperor; courtiers around the throne also smoothed his way.

sentences.zh: 帝怒漸解。

translations.literal: The emperor's anger gradually eased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger slowly subsided.

sentences.zh: 未幾，加少保，尋進兼文淵閣大學士，參預機務。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Junior Guardian, and soon advanced to concurrent Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion, participating in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made junior guardian, then grand secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion with a voice in policy.

sentences.zh: 密疏發咸寧侯仇鸞罪狀。

translations.literal: In a secret memorial he exposed the crimes of Marquis Qiu Luan of Xianning.
translations.idiomatic: In a secret memorial he exposed the crimes of Marquis Qiu Luan of Xianning.

sentences.zh: 嵩以階與鸞嘗同直，欲因鸞以傾階。

translations.literal: Song, because Jie had once served on duty together with Luan, wished to use Luan to overthrow Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Song hoped to use Luan—who had once served on duty with Jie—to bring Jie down.

sentences.zh: 及聞鸞罪發自階，乃愕然止，而忌階益甚。

translations.literal: When he learned that Luan's crimes had been exposed by Jie, he stopped in astonishment but resented Jie all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Jie had exposed Luan, he halted in shock but hated him all the more.

sentences.zh: 帝既誅鸞，益重階，數與謀邊事。

translations.literal: After the emperor had executed Luan, he valued Jie still more and often consulted him on frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Luan's execution the emperor valued Jie more highly and often consulted him on frontier policy.

sentences.zh: 時議減鸞所益衛卒，階言：「不可減。

translations.literal: At the time there was discussion of reducing the guard troops Luan had added; Jie said, "They must not be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated cutting the guard troops Luan had added, Jie said, "They must not be cut.

sentences.zh: 又京營積弱之故，卒不在乏而在冗，宜精汰之，取其廩以資賞費。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the long weakness of the capital garrisons lies not in too few soldiers but in redundancy; they should be carefully culled, and their grain rations turned to reward funds.
translations.idiomatic: The capital armies had grown weak not from too few men but from too many idle ones; he urged a careful purge and redirecting saved rations to rewards.

sentences.zh: 又請罷提督侍郎孫禬。

translations.literal: He also asked to abolish the post of supervising vice minister Sun Kai.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged abolishing the supervisory post held by Vice Minister Sun Kai.

sentences.zh: 帝始格於嵩，久而皆用之。

translations.literal: At first the emperor was blocked by Song, but in time he adopted all of Jie's proposals.
translations.idiomatic: At first Song blocked these ideas, but in time the emperor adopted them all.

sentences.zh: 一品滿三載，進勛，為柱國，再進兼太子太傅、武英殿大學士。

translations.literal: After three years at the first rank he was advanced in ennoblement to Pillar of the State, and again promoted to concurrent Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: After three years at the top rank he was ennobled Pillar of the State, then made grand tutor of the heir apparent and grand secretary of the Wuying Hall.

sentences.zh: 滿六載，兼食大學士俸，再錄子為中書舍人，加少傅。

translations.literal: After six years he drew concurrently the salary of a grand secretary, his son was again enrolled as a secretarial draftsman, and he was made Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: After six years he drew a second grand secretary's salary, his son was again enrolled as a drafting clerk, and he received the title of junior tutor.

sentences.zh: 九載，改兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was changed to concurrent Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In his ninth year he was given concurrent appointment as minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 賜宴禮部，璽書褒諭有加。

translations.literal: He was granted a banquet at the Ministry of Rites, and an imperial letter of praise with added commendation.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave him a banquet at the Ministry of Rites and an imperial letter of special praise.

sentences.zh: 帝雖重階，稍示形跡。

translations.literal: Although the emperor valued Jie, he showed slight signs of favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor still valued Jie, he began to show his preferences openly.

sentences.zh: 嘗以五色芝授嵩，使練藥，謂階政本所關，不以相及。

translations.literal: Once he gave five-colored lingzhi to Song to prepare medicine, saying that Jie was concerned with the foundations of government and should not be involved.
translations.idiomatic: Once he gave Song five-colored lingzhi to prepare elixirs, saying Jie handled the foundations of government and should not be bothered with such matters.

sentences.zh: 階皇恐請，乃得之。

translations.literal: Jie begged in terror and only then received some.
translations.idiomatic: Jie pleaded in alarm before he too was given a share.

sentences.zh: 帝亦漸委任階，亞於嵩。

translations.literal: The emperor also gradually entrusted affairs to Jie, second only to Song.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also came to rely on Jie, though still below Song.

sentences.zh: 楊繼盛諭嵩罪，以二王為徵，下錦衣獄。

translations.literal: Yang Jisheng enumerated Song's crimes, taking the two princes as evidence, and was cast into the Brocade Guard prison.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jisheng denounced Song's crimes, citing the two princes as proof, and was thrown into the Brocade Guard prison.

sentences.zh: 嵩屬陸炳究主使者。

translations.literal: Song ordered Lu Bing to investigate who was behind it.
translations.idiomatic: Song told Lu Bing to find who was behind the accusation.

sentences.zh: 階戒炳曰：「即不慎，一及皇子，如宗社何！」

translations.literal: Jie warned Bing, "If you are not careful and the inquiry touches the princes, what will become of the altars of state!
translations.idiomatic: Jie warned Bing, "One careless step that implicates the princes—what then becomes of the dynasty?

sentences.zh: 又為危語動嵩曰：「上惟二子，必不忍以謝公，所罪左右耳。

translations.literal: He also used alarming words to move Song: "The emperor has only these two sons; he will never sacrifice you to answer for this—the guilt will fall on those at your side.
translations.idiomatic: He also alarmed Song: "The emperor has only those two sons; he will never sacrifice you to settle this—the blame will fall on your retainers.

sentences.zh: 公奈何顯結宮邸怨也。」

translations.literal: Why should you, sir, openly incur the resentment of the princes' households?"
translations.idiomatic: Why openly make enemies of the princes' households?"

sentences.zh: 嵩忄雙懼，乃寢。

translations.literal: Song was terrified and dropped the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Song was terrified and let the case drop.

sentences.zh: 倭躪東南，帝數以問階，階力主發兵。

translations.literal: Japanese pirates ravaged the southeast; the emperor repeatedly asked Jie, and Jie strongly urged sending troops.
translations.idiomatic: As Japanese raiders ravaged the southeast, the emperor repeatedly consulted Jie, who strongly urged military action.

sentences.zh: 階又念邊卒苦飢，請收畿內麥數十萬石，自居庸輸宣府，紫荊輸大同。

translations.literal: Jie also thought of the frontier soldiers' bitter hunger and asked to collect several hundred thousand piculs of wheat from the capital region, shipping from Juyong to Xuanfu and from Zijing to Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of starving frontier troops, he proposed collecting hundreds of thousands of piculs of wheat from the capital region—shipping it from Juyong to Xuanfu and from Zijing to Datong.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，密傳諭行之。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and secretly transmitted orders to carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and secretly ordered it done.

sentences.zh: 楊繼盛之劾嵩也，嵩固疑階。

translations.literal: When Yang Jisheng impeached Song, Song had long suspected Jie.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jisheng attacked Song, Song had already suspected Jie was behind it.

sentences.zh: 趙錦、王宗茂劾嵩，階又議薄其罰。

translations.literal: Zhao Jin and Wang Zongmao impeached Song; Jie again argued for lenient punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Jin and Wang Zongmao attacked Yan Song, Jie again urged lighter penalties.

sentences.zh: 及是給事中吳時來、主事董傳策、張翀劾嵩不勝，皆下獄。

translations.literal: On this occasion the supervising secretary Wu Shilai and section chiefs Dong Chuance and Zhang Chong impeached Song without success and were all cast into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Then supervising secretary Wu Shilai and section chiefs Dong Chuance and Zhang Chong attacked Song and failed; all were imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 傳策，階裡人；

translations.literal: Chuance was a fellow townsman of Jie's;
translations.idiomatic: Chuance was from Jie's home district;

sentences.zh: 時來、翀，階門生也。

translations.literal: Shilai and Chong were Jie's disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Shilai and Chong were his students.

sentences.zh: 嵩遂疏辨，顯謂階主使，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Song then memorialized in defense, openly saying Jie was the mastermind; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Song countered in a memorial, openly accusing Jie of orchestrating the attacks; the emperor would not hear it.

sentences.zh: 有所密詢，皆舍嵩而之階。

translations.literal: Whenever there was a confidential inquiry, the emperor set Song aside and went to Jie.
translations.idiomatic: On confidential matters the emperor bypassed Song and turned to Jie.

sentences.zh: 尋加太子太師。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made grand preceptor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 帝所居永壽宮災，徙居玉熙殿，隘甚，欲有所營建，以問嵩。

translations.literal: The Yongshou Palace where the emperor lived burned; he moved to the Yuxi Hall, which was very cramped, and wished to undertake construction; he asked Song.
translations.idiomatic: When fire destroyed the Yongshou Palace, the emperor moved to the cramped Yuxi Hall and wanted to build anew; he asked Song.

sentences.zh: 嵩請還大內，帝不懌。

translations.literal: Song asked that he return to the inner palace; the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Song urged him back into the Forbidden City, which displeased him.

sentences.zh: 問階，階請以三殿所余材，責尚書雷禮營之，可計月而就。

translations.literal: He asked Jie; Jie asked to use leftover timber from the three main halls, charge Minister Lei Li with the work, and said it could be finished within a month.
translations.idiomatic: Asked Jie, he proposed using surplus timber from the three main halls and putting Minister Lei Li in charge—work that could finish within a month.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，如階議。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and followed Jie's plan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and followed Jie's plan.

sentences.zh: 命階子尚寶丞璠兼工部主事，董其役，十旬而功成。

translations.literal: He ordered Jie's son Fan, a director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, to serve concurrently as a section chief in the Ministry of Works and supervise the project; in a hundred days it was completed.
translations.idiomatic: He put Jie's son Fan, a director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, in charge as concurrent Works section chief; the project finished in a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 帝即日徙居之，命曰萬壽宮。

translations.literal: The emperor moved in that very day and named it the Wanshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor moved in the same day and named it the Palace of Long Life.

sentences.zh: 以階忠，進少師，兼支尚書俸，予一子中書舍人。

translations.literal: Because of Jie's loyalty he was advanced to Junior Preceptor, drew concurrently a minister's salary, and one son was granted status as a secretarial draftsman.
translations.idiomatic: For his loyalty Jie was made junior preceptor, drew a minister's salary as well, and a son was enrolled as a drafting clerk.

sentences.zh: 子璠亦超擢太常少卿。

translations.literal: His son Fan was also promoted out of turn to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fan was also leapfrogged to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 嵩乃日屈。

translations.literal: Song's position therefore declined day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Song's influence waned daily.

sentences.zh: 嵩子世蕃貪橫淫縱狀亦漸聞，階乃令御史鄒應龍劾之。

translations.literal: Reports also gradually spread of the greed, violence, and debauchery of Song's son Shifan; Jie then had Censor Zou Yinglong impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: As word spread of Shifan's greed and excess, Jie had censor Zou Yinglong impeach him.

sentences.zh: 帝勒嵩致仕，擢應龍通政司參議。

translations.literal: The emperor compelled Song to retire and promoted Yinglong to Secretariat Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor forced Song to retire and promoted Yinglong to a post in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 階遂代嵩為首輔。

translations.literal: Jie then replaced Song as chief grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Jie then replaced Song as chief grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 已而帝念嵩供奉勞，憐之。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor thought of Song's long service and pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the emperor remembered Song's years of service and felt pity.

sentences.zh: 又以調去，忽忽不樂，乃降諭，欲退而修真且傳嗣，復責階等奈何以官與邪物，謂應龍也。

translations.literal: Because Song had been removed, he grew restless and unhappy; he issued a decree saying he wished to withdraw to cultivate the Way and transmit the succession, and again blamed Jie and the others for giving office to an evil creature—meaning Yinglong.
translations.idiomatic: Depressed by Song's removal, he issued a decree saying he wished to retire to cultivate immortality and settle the succession, and blamed Jie for promoting the worthless Yinglong.

sentences.zh: 階言：「退而傳嗣，臣等不敢奉命。

translations.literal: Jie said, "To withdraw and transmit the succession—we your servants dare not obey such an order.
translations.idiomatic: Jie replied, "We dare not obey an order to abdicate and name an heir.

sentences.zh: 應龍之轉，乃二部奉旨行之。」

translations.literal: Yinglong's transfer was carried out by the two ministries on imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglong's promotion was carried out by the ministries on your order.

sentences.zh: 帝乃已。

translations.literal: The emperor then let the matter drop.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 帝以嵩在直久，而世蕃顧為奸於外，因命階無久直。

translations.literal: Because Song had been on duty so long while Shifan carried on villainy outside, the emperor ordered Jie not to remain on duty too long.
translations.idiomatic: Since Song had held long duty while Shifan schemed outside, the emperor told Jie not to stay on duty indefinitely.

sentences.zh: 階窺帝意，言苟為奸，在外猶在內，固請入直。

translations.literal: Jie perceived the emperor's intent and said that if one would do evil, it could be done outside as well as inside; he firmly asked to enter regular duty.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the emperor's mind, Jie said villains could scheme from outside as well as within and firmly asked to resume regular duty.

sentences.zh: 帝以嵩直廬賜階。

translations.literal: The emperor gave Jie Song's duty quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave Jie Song's duty quarters.

sentences.zh: 階榜三語其中曰：「以威福還主上，以政務還諸司，以用舍刑賞還公論。」

translations.literal: Jie posted three phrases there: "Return authority and favor to the sovereign, return administration to the ministries, return appointments and punishments to public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Jie posted three maxims there: "Return power to the throne, administration to the ministries, and appointments and punishments to public opinion.

sentences.zh: 於是朝士侃侃，得行其意。

translations.literal: Thereupon court officials spoke freely and were able to carry out their intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials spoke freely again and could act on their convictions.

sentences.zh: 袁煒數出直，階請召與共擬旨。

translations.literal: Yuan Wei often came on duty; Jie asked that he be summoned to draft rescripts together.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Wei came on duty, Jie asked that he join in drafting imperial rescripts.

sentences.zh: 因言：「事同眾則公，公則百美基；

translations.literal: He said, "When affairs are shared they are public; when public, a hundred virtues take root;
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Shared deliberation is public; public deliberation is the root of every good policy;

sentences.zh: 專則私，私則百弊生。」

translations.literal: when monopolized they are private; when private, a hundred abuses arise.
translations.idiomatic: monopoly is private, and private rule breeds a hundred abuses.

sentences.zh: 帝頷之。

translations.literal: The emperor nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded in agreement.

sentences.zh: 階以張孚敬及嵩導帝猜刻，力反之，務以寬大開帝意。

translations.literal: Jie, because Zhang Fuyi and Song had led the emperor toward suspicion and severity, strove against this and sought to open the emperor's mind through magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Zhang Fuyi and Song had made the emperor suspicious and harsh, Jie worked to soften him through magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 帝惡給事御史抨擊過當，欲有所行遣。

translations.literal: The emperor hated the excessive attacks of supervising secretaries and censors and wished to punish some.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor resented censors who attacked too fiercely and wanted to punish them.

sentences.zh: 階委曲調劑，得輕論。

translations.literal: Jie tactfully mediated so that lighter penalties were imposed.
translations.idiomatic: Jie mediated tactfully so lighter penalties were imposed.

sentences.zh: 會問階知人之難，階對曰：「大奸似忠，大詐似信。

translations.literal: Once when asked about the difficulty of knowing men, Jie replied, "Great villains seem loyal; great deceivers seem trustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about the difficulty of judging men, he said, "Great villains seem loyal; great deceivers seem trustworthy.

sentences.zh: 惟廣聽納，則窮凶極惡，人為我攖之；

translations.literal: Only by listening widely and accepting counsel will the utterly vicious be exposed by others on my behalf;
translations.idiomatic: Only by listening widely will others expose the utterly vicious for me;

sentences.zh: 深情隱慝，人為我發之。

translations.literal: deep schemes and hidden malice be brought to light by others on my behalf.
translations.idiomatic: and hidden schemes be brought to light by others for me.

sentences.zh: 故聖帝明王，有言必察。

translations.literal: Therefore sage emperors and enlightened kings examine every word spoken to them.
translations.idiomatic: That is why sage rulers examine every word spoken to them.

sentences.zh: 即不實，小者置之，大則薄責而容之，以鼓來者。」

translations.literal: Even if untrue, small matters are set aside; great ones receive light blame yet tolerance, to encourage those who come after.
translations.idiomatic: Even false reports: dismiss small ones, lightly rebuke large ones but tolerate them, to encourage future speakers.

sentences.zh: 帝稱善。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this as good.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the advice.

sentences.zh: 言路益發舒。

translations.literal: The avenue of speech became still more open.
translations.idiomatic: Free speech at court grew still more open.

sentences.zh: 寇由牆子嶺入，直趨通州。

translations.literal: The enemy entered by Qiangzi Ridge and drove straight for Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders entered through Qiangzi Ridge and drove straight for Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝方祠釐，兵部尚書楊博不敢奏，謀之階，檄宣府總兵官馬芳、宣大總督江東入援。

translations.literal: The emperor was performing ritual observances; Minister of War Yang Bo dared not memorialize and consulted Jie, who issued orders to Regional Commander Ma Fang of Xuanfu and Grand Coordinator Jiang Dong of Xuan-Da to enter with relief.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was at ritual observances, War Minister Yang Bo dared not report the crisis and consulted Jie, who ordered Ma Fang and Jiang Dong to march to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 芳兵先至，階請亟賞之，又請重東權，俾統諸道兵。

translations.literal: Fang's troops arrived first; Jie asked that they be rewarded at once and that Dong's authority be strengthened so he could command the armies of all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's troops arrived first; Jie urged immediate rewards and greater authority for Jiang Dong to command all relief forces.

sentences.zh: 寇從通掠香河，階請亟備順義，而以奇兵邀之古北口。

translations.literal: The enemy passed through Tongzhou and plundered Xianghe; Jie asked that Shunyi be prepared at once and that a surprise force intercept them at Gubeikou.
translations.idiomatic: As raiders swept from Tongzhou into Xianghe, Jie urged defenses at Shunyi and an ambush at Gubeikou.

sentences.zh: 寇趨順義，不得入，乃走古北口。

translations.literal: The enemy rushed toward Shunyi but could not enter and therefore fled toward Gubeikou.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders rushed Shunyi, failed to break in, and fled toward Gubeikou.

sentences.zh: 其後軍遇參將郭琥伏而敗，頗得其所掠人畜輜重。

translations.literal: Their rear guard met an ambush by Vice Commander Guo Hu and was defeated; much of the livestock, people, and baggage they had seized was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Their rear guard fell into Guo Hu's ambush and was routed; much loot was recovered.

sentences.zh: 始帝怒博不早聞與總督楊選之任寇入也，欲罪之未發。

translations.literal: At first the emperor was angry that Bo had not reported early and that Grand Coordinator Yang Xuan had let the enemy in, and wished to punish them but had not yet done so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious that Bo had not reported sooner and that Yang Xuan had let the enemy through, and was about to punish them.

sentences.zh: 階言：「博雖以祠釐禁不敢聞，而二鎮兵皆其所先檄。

translations.literal: Jie said, "Although Bo, because of the ritual prohibition, dared not report, the troops of both garrisons were mobilized on his prior orders.
translations.idiomatic: Jie said, "Bo could not report during the ritual prohibition, but he had already ordered both garrisons forward.

sentences.zh: 若選則非尾寇，乃送之出境耳。」

translations.literal: As for Xuan, he did not merely trail the enemy—he escorted them out of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan did not merely trail the enemy—he escorted them out of the realm.

sentences.zh: 帝竟誅選，不罪博。

translations.literal: The emperor in the end executed Xuan and did not punish Bo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor executed Xuan but spared Bo.

sentences.zh: 進階建極殿大學士。

translations.literal: Jie was advanced to Grand Secretary of the Jianji Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was promoted to grand secretary of the Jianji Hall.

sentences.zh: 袁煒以疾歸，道卒，階獨當國。

translations.literal: Yuan Wei returned home on account of illness and died on the road; Jie alone directed the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Wei fell ill on the road home and died; Jie alone directed the government.

sentences.zh: 屢請增閣臣，且乞骸骨。

translations.literal: He repeatedly asked to add grand secretaries and also begged to retire.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked to add colleagues to the Grand Secretariat and sought retirement.

sentences.zh: 乃命嚴訥、李春芳入閣，而待階益隆。

translations.literal: Yan Na and Li Chunfang were then ordered into the Grand Secretariat, while Jie was treated with still greater honor.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Na and Li Chunfang were brought into the Grand Secretariat while Jie was honored still more highly.

sentences.zh: 以一品十五載考，恩禮特厚，復賜玉帶、繡蟒、珍藥。

translations.literal: On the fifteen-year review of his first rank, favors were especially generous; he was again given a jade belt, embroidered python robes, and precious medicines.
translations.idiomatic: At his fifteen-year review at the top rank he received exceptional honors—again a jade belt, python robes, and precious medicines.

sentences.zh: 帝手書問階疾，諄懇如家人，階益恭謹。

translations.literal: The emperor wrote in his own hand to inquire after Jie's illness, as earnestly as a family member; Jie became still more respectful and careful.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote in his own hand to ask after Jie's health, as warmly as family; Jie became still more deferential.

sentences.zh: 帝或有所委，通夕不假寐，應制之文，未嘗逾頃刻期。

translations.literal: When the emperor entrusted him with tasks, he would go the whole night without sleep; compositions for imperial command never missed the deadline by so much as a moment.
translations.idiomatic: When entrusted with tasks he worked through the night; imperial compositions never missed their deadline.

sentences.zh: 帝日益愛階。

translations.literal: The emperor daily loved Jie more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's affection for him deepened daily.

sentences.zh: 階採輿論利便者，白而行之。

translations.literal: Jie gathered what public opinion deemed beneficial and, reporting it, put it into practice.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered sound proposals from public opinion and put them into practice.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中葉，南北用兵。

translations.literal: In the mid-Jiajing period warfare was waged north and south.
translations.idiomatic: In mid-Jiajing the empire fought wars north and south.

sentences.zh: 邊鎮大臣小不當帝指，輒逮下獄誅竄，閣臣復竊顏色為威福。

translations.literal: Frontier commanders who in the least failed to please the emperor were seized, imprisoned, executed, or banished, while grand secretaries again stole authority from his countenance to wield power and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier commanders who displeased the emperor were seized, imprisoned, or executed, while grand secretaries abused his moods for private power.

sentences.zh: 階當國後，緹騎省減，詔獄漸虛，任事者亦得以功名終。

translations.literal: After Jie directed the state, the brocade guards were reduced, the imperial prison gradually emptied, and those who took office could also end their careers with reputation intact.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jie the secret police were curbed, the imperial prison emptied, and officials could finish their careers with honor.

sentences.zh: 於是論者翕然推階為名相。

translations.literal: Thereupon commentators unanimously acclaimed Jie as a statesman of renown.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators hailed him as a statesman of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 給事、御史多起廢籍，恃階而強，言多過激。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries and censors, many raised from the rolls of the dismissed, relied on Jie and grew bold; their words were often excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Many censors restored from dismissal relied on Jie and spoke with excessive harshness.

sentences.zh: 帝不能堪，諭階等處之。

translations.literal: The emperor could not bear it and instructed Jie and the others to deal with them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not endure it and told Jie to handle them.

sentences.zh: 同列欲擬譴，階曰：「上欲譴，我曹當力爭，乃可導之譴乎。」

translations.literal: His colleagues wished to draft reprimands; Jie said, "If the emperor wishes to reprimand, we ought to strive against it—how can we lead him to reprimand them?
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues wanted formal reprimands; Jie said, "If the emperor wants to punish them, we should resist—not help him punish.

sentences.zh: 請傳諭令省改。

translations.literal: He asked that a transmitted order tell them to reflect and reform.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that they be told privately to moderate their tone.

sentences.zh: 帝亦勿之罪。

translations.literal: The emperor also did not punish them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not punish them.

sentences.zh: 是年，詔翰林撰中秋宴致語，階言：「先帝未撤几筵，不可宴樂。」

translations.literal: That year an edict ordered the Hanlin to compose banquet addresses for the Mid-Autumn Festival; Jie said, "The late emperor's spirit tablet has not yet been removed—there can be no feasting and music.
translations.idiomatic: That year the court ordered Mid-Autumn banquet addresses; Jie said, "The late emperor's mourning rites are not finished—there can be no feast.

sentences.zh: 帝為罷宴。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore canceled the banquet.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor canceled the banquet.

sentences.zh: 帝命中官分督團營，階力陳不可而止。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered eunuchs to supervise the camp divisions separately; Jie strongly argued that this could not be done, and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor ordered eunuchs to supervise army camps separately, Jie argued fiercely until the order was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 南京振武營兵屢嘩，階欲汰之。

translations.literal: The troops of the Zhenwu Camp in Nanjing repeatedly mutinied; Jie wished to reduce their numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Troops of Nanjing's Zhenwu Camp mutinied repeatedly; Jie wanted to reduce their numbers.

sentences.zh: 慮其據孝陵不可攻也，先令操江都御史唐繼錄督江防兵駐陵傍，而徐下兵部分散之。

translations.literal: Fearing that if they seized the Xiaoling mausoleum they could not be attacked, he first had Tang Jilu, censor in charge of the Yangzi defense, station river-defense troops beside the tomb, then gradually sent down orders for the military commissions to disperse them.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing they might seize the imperial mausoleum and become unassailable, he first stationed river-defense troops nearby, then gradually dispersed them through the military commissions.

sentences.zh: 事遂定。

translations.literal: The affair was thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: The crisis was settled.

sentences.zh: 群小璫毆御史於午門，都御史王廷將糾之，階曰：「不得主名，劾何益？

translations.literal: Petty eunuchs beat a censor at the Meridian Gate; Censor-in-Chief Wang Ting was about to impeach them; Jie said, "Without the culprits' names, what good is impeachment?
translations.idiomatic: Petty eunuchs beat a censor at the Meridian Gate; when Wang Ting prepared to impeach them, Jie said, "Without names, impeachment is useless.

sentences.zh: 且慮彼先誣我。」

translations.literal: Moreover I fear they will accuse us first.
translations.idiomatic: They may accuse us first.

sentences.zh: 乃使人以好語誘大璫，先錄其主名。

translations.literal: He therefore sent someone with friendly words to coax a senior eunuch and first record the names of the ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: He sent someone to coax a senior eunuch with friendly words and record the ringleaders' names.

sentences.zh: 廷疏上，乃分別逮治有差。

translations.literal: When Ting's memorial went up, they were arrested and punished separately according to degree.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Ting's memorial went up, the culprits were arrested and punished according to their roles.

sentences.zh: 階之持正應變，多此類也。

translations.literal: Jie's uprightness and resourcefulness were mostly of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Jie's integrity and resourcefulness took many such forms.

sentences.zh: 階所持諍，多宮禁事，行者十八九，中官多側目。

translations.literal: Most of the remonstrances Jie offered concerned palace matters; eight or nine in ten were carried out, and many eunuchs regarded him with hostility.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his remonstrances concerned palace affairs; the emperor accepted most of them, and many eunuchs resented him.

sentences.zh: 會帝幸南海子，階諫，不從。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited the Southern Park, Jie remonstrated but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited the Southern Park, Jie remonstrated in vain.

sentences.zh: 方乞休，而給事中張齊以私怨劾階，階因請歸。

translations.literal: He was just then asking to retire when the supervising secretary Zhang Qi impeached him out of private resentment; Jie therefore asked to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He was seeking retirement when Zhang Qi attacked him out of private spite; Jie asked to go home.

sentences.zh: 帝意亦漸移，許之。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind had also gradually shifted, and he granted permission.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mind had shifted, and he agreed.

sentences.zh: 賜馳驛。

translations.literal: He was granted post-horse service.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted imperial post horses.

sentences.zh: 以春芳請，給夫廩，璽書褒美，行人導行，如故事。

translations.literal: At Li Chunfang's request he was given porters and grain allowance, an imperial letter of praise, and an envoy to guide him on the road, according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: At Li Chunfang's request he received porters, grain allowance, an imperial letter of praise, and an escort home by precedent.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，賜白金、寶鈔、彩幣、襲衣。

translations.literal: At his farewell audience he was given silver, treasure notes, silks, and ceremonial robes.
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience he received silver, treasure notes, silks, and ceremonial robes.

sentences.zh: 舉朝皆疏留，報聞而已。

translations.literal: The whole court memorialized to retain him; the reply was merely acknowledgment.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court memorialized to keep him; the emperor merely acknowledged receipt.

sentences.zh: 王廷後刺得張齊納賄事，劾戍之邊。

translations.literal: Wang Ting later uncovered Zhang Qi's acceptance of bribes and impeached him to border exile.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ting later exposed Zhang Qi's bribery and had him exiled to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 階既行，春芳為首輔，未幾亦歸。

translations.literal: After Jie had left, Chunfang became chief grand secretary; before long he too returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After Jie left, Li Chunfang became chief minister; soon he too retired.

sentences.zh: 拱再出，扼階不遺餘力。

translations.literal: When Gong returned to power, he strove to the utmost to crush Jie.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Gong returned to power, he attacked Jie without restraint.

sentences.zh: 郡邑有司希拱指，爭齮晷階，盡奪其田，戍其二子。

translations.literal: Local officials, eager to follow Gong's intent, vied to slander Jie, seized all his land, and banished his two sons to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials eager to please Gong seized his lands and exiled his two sons.

sentences.zh: 會拱復為居正所傾而罷，事乃解。

translations.literal: When Gong in turn was overthrown by Juzheng and dismissed, the matter was resolved.
translations.idiomatic: When Gong was in turn ousted by Zhang Juzheng, the persecution ended.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十年，階年八十，詔遣行人存問，賜璽書、金幣。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Wanli, when Jie was eighty, an edict sent an envoy to inquire after him and bestowed an imperial letter, gold, and silks.
translations.idiomatic: In 1582, when Jie was eighty, the throne sent an envoy with an imperial letter, gold, and silks.

sentences.zh: 明年卒。

translations.literal: The next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year.

sentences.zh: 贈太師，諡文貞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous title Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand preceptor with the posthumous title Wenzhen, "Cultivated and Steadfast."

sentences.zh: 階立朝有相度，保全善類。

translations.literal: Jie in office had the measure of a statesman and preserved men of worth.
translations.idiomatic: In office Jie showed true statesmanship and protected good men.

sentences.zh: 嘉、隆之政，多所匡救。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing and Longqing reigns he corrected and rescued much in government.
translations.idiomatic: He corrected many abuses of the Jiajing and Longqing reigns.

sentences.zh: 間有委蛇，亦不失大節。

translations.literal: At times he was accommodating, yet he never lost his great integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He could be flexible when circumstances required, but he never abandoned his fundamental principles.

sentences.zh: 弟 陟

translations.literal: Younger brother: Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Sheng.

sentences.zh: 子 璠 等

translations.literal: Sons: Fan and others.
translations.idiomatic: His sons included Fan and others.

sentences.zh: 階弟陟，嘉靖二十六年進士。

translations.literal: Jie's younger brother Sheng passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: Jie's younger brother Sheng became a jinshi in 1547.

sentences.zh: 累官南京刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Through successive offices he rose to Vice Minister of Justice at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to become vice minister of justice at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 子璠，以廕官太常卿；

translations.literal: His son Fan, through yin privilege, became Chief Ritual Official of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: His son Fan entered office by yin privilege and became chief ritual official of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 琨、瑛，尚寶卿。

translations.literal: Kun and Ying were Directors of the Imperial Seal.
translations.idiomatic: Kun and Ying served as directors of the imperial seal.

sentences.zh: 孫元春，進士，亦官太常卿。

translations.literal: His grandson Yuanchun, a jinshi, also served as Chief Ritual Official.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yuanchun, also a jinshi, held the same post of chief ritual official.

sentences.zh: 元春孫本高，官錦衣千戶，天啟中拒魏忠賢建祠奪職。

translations.literal: Yuanchun's grandson Bengao served as a battalion commander in the Embroidered Uniform Guard; during the Tianqi reign he refused Wei Zhongxian's temple-building and was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchun's grandson Bengao was a battalion commander in the Embroidered Uniform Guard; under Tianqi he refused to support Wei Zhongxian's temple project and lost his post.

sentences.zh: 崇禎改元，以薦起，累官左都督。

translations.literal: When the Chongzhen era began, he was recalled by recommendation and rose through offices to Left Chief Commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Chongzhen reign he was recalled on recommendation and eventually rose to left chief commander.

sentences.zh: 諸生念祖，國變城破，與妻張，二妾陸、李，皆自縊。

translations.literal: The licentiate Nianzu, when the dynasty fell and the city was taken, together with his wife Zhang and two concubines, Lu and Li, all hanged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The licentiate Nianzu, when the dynasty collapsed and the city fell, hanged himself along with his wife Zhang and his two concubines, Lu and Li.

sentences.zh: 高拱，字肅卿，新鄭人。

translations.literal: Gao Gong, style Suqing, was a native of Xinzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gong, whose style was Suqing, came from Xinzheng.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twentieth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in 1541.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士。

translations.literal: He was selected as a bachelor in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was chosen as a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 逾年，授編修。

translations.literal: After a year he was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made a compiler.

sentences.zh: 穆宗居裕邸，出閣請讀，拱與檢討陳以勤併為侍講。

translations.literal: When Muzong lived at the Prince of Yu residence and left the palace to begin his studies, Gong and Proofreader Chen Yiqin were jointly appointed lecture companions.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Muzong was lodged at the Prince of Yu's residence and began formal study outside the inner palace, Gong and Chen Yiqin were appointed together as his lecture companions.

sentences.zh: 世宗諱言立太子，而景王未之國，中外危疑。

translations.literal: Shizong avoided speaking of establishing the crown prince, and the Prince of Jing had not yet gone to his fief, so court and country were filled with fear and doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong refused even to discuss naming an heir, and since the Prince of Jing had not yet left for his fief, the court and the realm were racked with uncertainty.

sentences.zh: 拱侍裕邸九年，啟王益敦孝謹，敷陳剴切。

translations.literal: Gong served at the Prince of Yu residence for nine years, instructing the prince to be ever more filial and cautious, and expounding with earnest directness.
translations.idiomatic: Gong served at the Prince of Yu residence for nine years, urging the prince toward greater filial devotion and restraint and instructing him with forceful clarity.

sentences.zh: 王甚重之，手書「懷賢忠貞」字賜焉。

translations.literal: The prince greatly valued him and personally wrote the characters "Cherishing Worth, Loyal and Steadfast" as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: The prince held him in high esteem and personally wrote the words "Cherishing Worth, Loyal and Steadfast" as a gift.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍講學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to reader-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 嚴嵩、徐階遞當國，以拱他日當得重，薦之世宗。

translations.literal: Yan Song and Xu Jie successively held power; because Gong would one day hold great authority, they recommended him to Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song and Xu Jie each held the reins of government in turn, and both recommended Gong to Shizong, judging that he would one day wield great influence.

sentences.zh: 拜太常卿，掌國子監祭酒事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Ritual Official and directed the duties of Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief ritual official and placed in charge of the chancellor's duties at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，擢禮部左侍郎。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year he was promoted to Left Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 1562 he was promoted to left vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 尋改吏部，兼學士，掌詹事府事。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, concurrently served as Grand Secretary, and oversaw the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to the Ministry of Personnel, made a grand secretary as well, and put in charge of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 進禮部尚書，召入直廬。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister of Rites and summoned to serve in the duty quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of rites and summoned to take up duty at the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 撰齋詞，賜飛魚服。

translations.literal: He composed fasting texts and was granted flying-fish robes.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted fasting liturgies and was rewarded with flying-fish robes.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，拜文淵閣大學士，與郭樸同入閣。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion and entered the cabinet together with Guo Pu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1566 he was made grand secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion and entered the cabinet alongside Guo Pu.

sentences.zh: 拱與樸皆階所薦也。

translations.literal: Both Gong and Pu had been recommended by Xu Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Both Gong and Pu had been Xu Jie's protégés.

sentences.zh: 世宗居西苑，閣臣直廬在苑中。

translations.literal: Shizong resided in the Western Park, and the grand secretaries' duty quarters were within the park.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong lived in the Western Park, and the grand secretaries' duty quarters were inside it.

sentences.zh: 拱未有子，移家近直廬，時竊出。

translations.literal: Gong still had no son; he moved his household near the duty quarters and would slip out from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Gong had no son yet, so he moved his family close to the duty quarters and would slip away from time to time.

sentences.zh: 一日，帝不豫，誤傳非常，拱遽移具出。

translations.literal: One day the emperor was unwell; a false report of something extraordinary spread, and Gong hurriedly moved his belongings out.
translations.idiomatic: One day, when the emperor fell ill, a false rumor of crisis spread, and Gong hastily moved his household goods out of the quarters.

sentences.zh: 始階甚親拱，引入直。

translations.literal: At first Jie was very close to Gong and brought him into the duty roster.
translations.idiomatic: At first Xu Jie had been very close to Gong and had brought him into palace service.

sentences.zh: 拱驟貴，負氣頗忤階。

translations.literal: Gong suddenly rose to high rank, was proud by nature, and to a considerable degree offended Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gong's rise was sudden, his proud temperament increasingly put him at odds with Xu Jie.

sentences.zh: 給事中胡應嘉，階鄉人也，以劾拱姻親自危。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Hu Yingjia, a fellow townsman of Jie, impeached Gong's relatives by marriage and thereby put himself in danger.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yingjia, a supervising secretary and fellow townsman of Xu Jie, impeached Gong's relatives by marriage and thereby courted danger for himself.

sentences.zh: 且瞷階方與拱郤，遂劾拱不守直廬，移器用於外。

translations.literal: Moreover, seeing that Jie was at odds with Gong, he then impeached Gong for not keeping to the duty quarters and for moving his household goods outside.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Xu Jie and Gong were already estranged, he went on to accuse Gong of abandoning the duty quarters and moving his belongings out.

sentences.zh: 世宗病，勿省也。

translations.literal: Shizong was ill and did not review the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong was ill and took no notice of it.

sentences.zh: 拱疑應嘉受階指，大憾之。

translations.literal: Gong suspected that Yingjia had acted on Jie's instructions and greatly resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Gong believed Yingjia had been acting on Xu Jie's orders and was deeply embittered.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，進少保兼太子太保。

translations.literal: When Muzong ascended the throne, Gong was promoted to Junior Guardian and concurrently Junior Guardian of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong took the throne, Gong was promoted to junior guardian and concurrently junior guardian of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 階雖為首輔，而拱自以帝舊臣，數與之抗，樸復助之，階漸不能堪。

translations.literal: Though Jie was chief minister, Gong regarded himself as the emperor's old tutor and repeatedly opposed him; Pu again supported him, and Jie gradually could not endure it.
translations.idiomatic: Although Xu Jie was chief minister, Gong considered himself the emperor's former tutor and repeatedly challenged him; Guo Pu backed him, and Xu Jie found the situation increasingly unbearable.

sentences.zh: 而是時以勤與張居正皆入閣，居正亦侍裕邸講。

translations.literal: But at this time Chen Yiqin and Zhang Juzheng both entered the cabinet; Juzheng had also lectured at the Prince of Yu residence.
translations.idiomatic: By then Chen Yiqin and Zhang Juzheng had both entered the cabinet, and Juzheng too had served as a tutor at the Prince of Yu residence.

sentences.zh: 階草遺詔，獨與居正計，拱心彌不平。

translations.literal: Jie drafted the deathbed edict, planning only with Juzheng, and Gong's resentment grew ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jie drafted the deathbed edict in consultation with Zhang Juzheng alone, which only deepened Gong's resentment.

sentences.zh: 會議登極賞軍及請上裁去留大臣事，階悉不從拱議，嫌益深。

translations.literal: When they deliberated on rewards for troops at the accession and on asking the emperor to decide which ministers should stay or go, Jie rejected all of Gong's proposals, and their enmity deepened further.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated accession rewards for the army and which ministers the emperor should retain or dismiss, Xu Jie rejected every proposal Gong made, and their feud grew worse.

sentences.zh: 應嘉掌吏科，佐部院考察，事將竣，忽有所論救。

translations.literal: Yingjia headed the personnel section of the censorate and assisted the ministries and courts in the evaluation; when the business was nearly finished, he suddenly petitioned to save someone.
translations.idiomatic: Yingjia, who headed the personnel section of the censorate, was assisting the ministries in their evaluations when, just as the work was nearly complete, he suddenly intervened on someone's behalf.

sentences.zh: 帝責其牴牾，下閣臣議罰。

translations.literal: The emperor reproached him for obstruction and referred the matter of punishment to the grand secretaries for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him for obstruction and sent the matter to the grand secretaries to decide his punishment.

sentences.zh: 樸奮然曰：「應嘉無人臣禮，當編氓。」

translations.literal: Pu said passionately: "Yingjia lacks the decorum of a minister; he should be reduced to commoner status."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu declared heatedly, "Yingjia has no sense of a minister's duty and ought to be struck from the rolls and made a commoner."

sentences.zh: 階旁睨拱，見拱方怒，勉從之。

translations.literal: Jie glanced sideways at Gong, saw that Gong was angry, and reluctantly went along.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jie glanced at Gong, saw that he was furious, and reluctantly agreed.

sentences.zh: 言路謂拱以私怨逐應嘉，交章劾之。

translations.literal: The remonstrance officials said Gong had driven out Yingjia out of personal spite, and they submitted impeachments one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials charged that Gong had expelled Yingjia out of private spite, and memorial after memorial was submitted against him.

sentences.zh: 給事中歐陽一敬劾拱尤力。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Ouyang Yijing impeached Gong with particular force.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Yijing, a supervising secretary, attacked Gong with especial vigor.

sentences.zh: 階於拱辯疏，擬旨慰留，而不甚譴言者。

translations.literal: In response to Gong's defense memorial, Jie drafted a rescript to comfort and retain him, but did not strongly punish the accusers.
translations.idiomatic: When Gong submitted a defense, Xu Jie drafted a rescript reassuring him and keeping him in office, but did not punish his critics severely.

sentences.zh: 拱益怒，相與忿詆閣中。

translations.literal: Gong grew angrier still, and they hurled angry abuse at each other within the cabinet.
translations.idiomatic: Gong grew still angrier, and within the cabinet they exchanged furious recriminations.

sentences.zh: 御史齊康為拱劾階，康坐黜。

translations.literal: The censor Qi Kang impeached Jie on Gong's behalf, and Kang was dismissed as punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Qi Kang, acting for Gong, impeached Xu Jie, and Qi Kang himself was dismissed in consequence.

sentences.zh: 於是言路論拱者無虛日，南京科道至拾遺及之。

translations.literal: From then on the remonstrance officials criticized Gong without a single idle day; the censorate officials of Nanjing even brought up long-forgotten matters against him.
translations.idiomatic: After that, censorial attacks on Gong came almost daily, and the Nanjing censorate even dredged up old grievances against him.

sentences.zh: 拱不自安，乞歸，遂以少傅兼太子太傅、尚書、大學士養病去。

translations.literal: Gong felt insecure, sought to retire, and left on grounds of illness as Junior Mentor, concurrently Junior Mentor of the Crown Prince, Minister, and Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy in office, Gong asked to retire and left on grounds of illness, retaining the titles of junior mentor, junior mentor of the crown prince, minister, and grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年五月也。

translations.literal: This was in the fifth month of the first year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the fifth month of 1567.

sentences.zh: 拱以舊學蒙眷注，性強直自遂，頗快恩怨，卒不安其位去。

translations.literal: Gong, favored as the emperor's former tutor, was forceful and self-willed by nature and rather quick to settle scores of gratitude and resentment; in the end he left without securing his position.
translations.idiomatic: Favored as the emperor's old tutor, Gong was forceful and self-willed by nature and rather quick to settle old scores; in the end he could not hold his place and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 既而階亦乞歸。

translations.literal: Before long Jie also requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Xu Jie too asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，帝召拱以大學士兼掌吏部事。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year the emperor recalled Gong as Grand Secretary concurrently in charge of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year of Longqing the emperor recalled Gong as grand secretary and put him in charge of the Ministry of Personnel as well.

sentences.zh: 拱乃盡反階所為，凡先朝得罪諸臣以遺詔錄用贈恤者，一切報罷。

translations.literal: Gong then completely reversed what Jie had done; all former ministers who had been restored, posthumously honored, or granted relief through the deathbed edict were entirely struck down.
translations.idiomatic: Gong then overturned everything Xu Jie had done, canceling every restoration, posthumous honor, and grant of relief that the deathbed edict had bestowed on ministers punished in the previous reign.

sentences.zh: 且上疏極論之曰：「《明倫大典》頒示已久。

translations.literal: Moreover he submitted a memorial arguing forcefully, saying: "The Grand Canon of Bright Moral Relations has long been promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a forceful memorial arguing that "the Grand Canon of Bright Moral Relations has been in force for a long time.

sentences.zh: 今議事之臣假托詔旨，凡議禮得罪者悉從褒顯，將使獻皇在廟之靈何以為享？

translations.literal: Now the ministers deliberating have used the edict as a pretext; all who were punished over the rites dispute are to be commended and displayed. How will the spirit of Xianhuang in the temple receive its sacrifice?
translations.idiomatic: Now the ministers who deliberate policy are using the edict as a pretext to commend and rehabilitate everyone punished in the rites controversy. How can the spirit of Xianhuang in the ancestral temple accept its offerings?

sentences.zh: 先帝在天之靈何以為心？

translations.literal: How will the spirit of the late emperor in heaven be at heart?
translations.idiomatic: What will the late emperor's spirit in heaven make of this?

sentences.zh: 而陛下歲時入廟，亦何以對越二聖？

translations.literal: And when Your Majesty enters the temple at the yearly rites, how will you face the two sages?
translations.idiomatic: And when Your Majesty enters the temple at the seasonal sacrifices, how will you answer before the two imperial spirits?

sentences.zh: 臣以為未可。」

translations.literal: Your subject considers this inadmissible."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject believes this cannot be allowed.

sentences.zh: 帝深然之。

translations.literal: The emperor strongly agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 法司坐方士王金等子弒父律。

translations.literal: The judicial offices convicted the Daoist Wang Jin and others under the statute on sons killing their fathers.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial offices convicted the Daoist Wang Jin and his associates under the statute punishing a son who kills his father.

sentences.zh: 拱覆上疏曰：「人君隕於非命，不得正終，其名至不美。

translations.literal: Gong submitted a reply memorial, saying: "When a ruler dies by violent means and cannot end his life properly, the name is most unseemly.
translations.idiomatic: Gong submitted a reply memorial saying, "When a ruler dies by violence and cannot end his life properly, the reputation is utterly unspeakable.

sentences.zh: 先帝臨御四十五載，得歲六十有餘。

translations.literal: The late emperor reigned for forty-five years and reached more than sixty years of age.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor reigned for forty-five years and lived to more than sixty.

sentences.zh: 末年抱病，經歲上賓，壽考令終，曾無暴遽。

translations.literal: In his later years he was ill; after a year he passed away—a blessed old age and a proper end, without any sudden violence.
translations.idiomatic: In his final years he was ill; after a year he passed away—a long life and a proper end, with nothing sudden about it.

sentences.zh: 今謂先帝為王金所害，誣以不得正終，天下後世視先帝為何如主？

translations.literal: Now to say the late emperor was harmed by Wang Jin is to slander him with an improper end. What kind of ruler will the world and posterity take the late emperor to have been?
translations.idiomatic: To say now that the late emperor was killed by Wang Jin is to slander him with an improper death. What kind of ruler will the world and posterity think he was?

sentences.zh: 乞下法司改議。」

translations.literal: I beg that the judicial offices be ordered to reconsider."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the judicial offices be ordered to revise their finding.

sentences.zh: 帝復然拱言，命減戍。

translations.literal: The emperor again agreed with Gong's words and ordered the sentence reduced from exile.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again agreed with Gong and ordered the sentence reduced from exile.

sentences.zh: 拱之再出，專與階修郤，所論皆欲以中階重其罪。

translations.literal: Gong's second return was devoted solely to settling his feud with Jie; everything he proposed was aimed at hitting Jie and increasing his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: On his second return to power Gong devoted himself chiefly to settling his feud with Xu Jie; every proposal he made was intended to strike at Jie and magnify his offenses.

sentences.zh: 賴帝仁柔，弗之竟也。

translations.literal: Thanks to the emperor's gentle nature, he did not carry it through to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Only the emperor's mild temperament kept matters from going that far.

sentences.zh: 階子弟頗橫鄉里。

translations.literal: Jie's sons and younger relatives were rather overbearing in their home district.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jie's sons and younger kinsmen had become quite overbearing in their home district.

sentences.zh: 拱以前知府蔡國熙為監司，簿錄其諸子，皆編戍。

translations.literal: Gong appointed the former prefect Cai Guoxi as surveillance commissioner; he inventoried Jie's sons, and all were banished to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: Gong sent the former prefect Cai Guoxi as surveillance commissioner to inventory Xu Jie's sons, and all were banished to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 所以扼階者，無不至。

translations.literal: In every way of constraining Jie, nothing was left undone.
translations.idiomatic: There was no measure he did not use to squeeze Xu Jie.

sentences.zh: 逮拱去位，乃得解。

translations.literal: Only when Gong left office was relief obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Gong left office did the pressure ease.

sentences.zh: 拱練習政體，負經濟才，所建白皆可行。

translations.literal: Gong was practiced in the forms of government, possessed talent for statecraft, and every proposal he made could be implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Gong understood the workings of government, had genuine talent for statecraft, and every proposal he made was practical.

sentences.zh: 其在吏部，欲遍識人才，授諸司以籍，使署賢否，志里姓氏，月要而歲會之。

translations.literal: While at the Ministry of Personnel, he wished to know all talent comprehensively; he handed each department registers, had them note worthy and unworthy men and record their native places and surnames, and required monthly summaries and annual assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: At the Ministry of Personnel he sought to know the full roster of talent: he gave each department registers in which to mark men as worthy or unworthy and record their native places and surnames, with monthly summaries and an annual review.

sentences.zh: 倉卒舉用，皆得其人。

translations.literal: When men were urgently selected for appointment, the right persons were always found.
translations.idiomatic: Even when appointments had to be made in haste, the right men were always found.

sentences.zh: 又以時方憂邊事，請增置兵部侍郎，以儲總督之選。

translations.literal: Also, as border affairs were then a concern, he requested adding Vice Ministers of War to stock the pool for grand coordinator selections.
translations.idiomatic: Because border affairs were then pressing, he also asked to add vice ministers of war to build up a reserve pool for grand coordinator appointments.

sentences.zh: 由侍郎而總督，由總督而本兵，中外更番，邊材自裕。

translations.literal: From vice minister to grand coordinator, from grand coordinator to minister of war—rotation between central and frontier posts would naturally make border talent abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Promotion from vice minister to grand coordinator, and from grand coordinator to minister of war, with rotation between court and frontier, would naturally produce an ample supply of border talent.

sentences.zh: 又以兵者專門之學，非素習不可應卒。

translations.literal: He also held that warfare is a specialized discipline; without long training one cannot respond to emergencies.
