translations.idiomatic: He also argued that warfare is a specialized art and that without long training one cannot meet sudden emergencies.

sentences.zh: 儲養本兵，當自兵部司屬始。

translations.literal: Cultivating ministers of war should begin with the departmental staff of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Training future ministers of war should begin with the Ministry of War's own staff.

sentences.zh: 宜慎選司屬，多得智謀才力曉暢軍旅者，久而任之，勿遷他曹。

translations.literal: Departmental staff should be carefully selected, mostly men of wisdom, strategy, ability, and familiarity with military affairs; they should serve long and not be transferred to other offices.
translations.idiomatic: Staff should be chosen with care, favoring men of intelligence, strategy, ability, and military experience; they should serve long terms and not be transferred to other departments.

sentences.zh: 他日邊方兵備督撫之選，皆於是取之。

translations.literal: In future, selections for frontier military defense commissioners and governors should all be drawn from these.
translations.idiomatic: Future appointments to frontier defense and governorships should all be drawn from this pool.

sentences.zh: 更各取邊地之人以備司屬，如銓司分省故事，則題覆情形可無扞格，並重其賞罰以鼓勵之。

translations.literal: Further, men from each frontier region should be taken to fill the departmental staff, as in the old custom of the personnel office dividing by province; then memorials and replies would meet without obstruction, and rewards and punishments should be weighted to encourage them.
translations.idiomatic: Men from each frontier region should also be recruited for staff posts, following the old practice of dividing personnel work by province, so that memorials and replies would not be at cross purposes; rewards and punishments should be strengthened to encourage them.

sentences.zh: 凡邊地有司，其責頗重，不宜付雜流及遷謫者。

translations.literal: For all frontier prefects and magistrates, the responsibility is quite weighty; such posts should not be entrusted to miscellaneous appointees or those demoted and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier prefects and magistrates bear heavy responsibility and should not be entrusted to miscellaneous appointees or men under demotion and transfer.

sentences.zh: 皆報可，著為令。

translations.literal: All were approved and written as regulations.
translations.idiomatic: All of these proposals were approved and promulgated as regulations.

sentences.zh: 拱又奏請科貢與進士並用，勿循資格。

translations.literal: Gong also memorialized that tribute graduates and jinshi be used together, without rigid adherence to seniority rules.
translations.idiomatic: Gong also memorialized that tribute graduates and jinshi be employed together, without slavish adherence to seniority.

sentences.zh: 其在部考察，多所參伍，不盡憑文書為黜陟，亦不拘人數多寡，黜者必告以故，使眾咸服。

translations.literal: In his ministry evaluations he compared many factors and did not rely wholly on documents for promotions and demotions; he also did not fix the number to be dismissed; those dismissed were always told the reason so all would be convinced.
translations.idiomatic: In his ministry evaluations he weighed many factors and did not rely solely on paperwork for promotions and demotions; he also did not fix a quota for dismissals, and those dismissed were always told why, so that all were persuaded.

sentences.zh: 古田瑤賊亂，用殷正茂總督兩廣。

translations.literal: When Yao bandits rebelled in Gutian, Yin Zhengmao was appointed grand coordinator of the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao rebels rose in Gutian, he appointed Yin Zhengmao grand coordinator of Guangdong and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 曰：「是雖貪，可以集事。」

translations.literal: He said: "Though this man is greedy, he can get things done."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Greedy though he is, he can get things done.

sentences.zh: 貴州撫臣奏土司安國亨將叛，命阮文中代為巡撫。

translations.literal: The Guizhou governor reported that the native official An Guoheng was about to rebel, and Ruan Wenzhong was appointed to replace him as grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: When the Guizhou governor reported that the native chieftain An Guoheng was about to rebel, he appointed Ruan Wenzhong to replace him as grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 臨行語之曰：「國亨必不叛，若往，無激變也。」

translations.literal: Before his departure he told him: "Guoheng will certainly not rebel; when you go, do not provoke an incident."
translations.idiomatic: Before Ruan left, Gong told him, "Guoheng will not rebel; when you arrive, do not provoke trouble.

sentences.zh: 即而如其言。

translations.literal: Soon after, it happened just as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 以廣東有司多貪黷，特請旌廉能知府侯必登，以歷其餘。

translations.literal: Because Guangdong officials were largely corrupt, he specially requested honoring the incorrupt and capable prefect Hou Bideng to admonish the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Because so many Guangdong officials were corrupt, he specially recommended honoring the upright and capable prefect Hou Bideng as an example to the rest.

sentences.zh: 又言馬政、鹽政之官，名為卿、為使，而實以閒局視之，失人廢事，漸不可訓。

translations.literal: He also said that officials of horse policy and salt policy, though titled as directors and commissioners, were in fact treated as idle posts; men were wasted, business abandoned, and the practice gradually became unreformable.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that the officials in charge of horse policy and salt policy, though titled directors and commissioners, were treated in practice as sinecures; talent was wasted, business neglected, and the custom had become a bad precedent.

sentences.zh: 惟教官驛遞諸司，職卑錄薄，遠道為難，宜銓注近地，以恤其私。

translations.literal: Only for education officers, courier posts, and similar offices—low in rank and thin in compensation—serving far from home was hard; appointments should favor nearby places to show consideration for their private circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: For education officers, courier offices, and the like, whose posts were low in rank and pay and for whom distant assignment was a hardship, he urged that appointments be made close to home as a measure of consideration.

sentences.zh: 詔皆從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved all of these.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved all of these proposals.

sentences.zh: 拱所經畫，皆此類也。

translations.literal: The policies Gong planned were all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gong's plans were all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 俺答孫把漢那吉來降，總督王崇古受之，請於朝，乞授以官。

translations.literal: Altan Khan's grandson Ba Han Naji came to surrender; Grand Coordinator Wang Chonggu accepted him, reported to court, and requested that he be granted an office.
translations.idiomatic: Altan Khan's grandson Ba Han Naji came over to the Ming side; Grand Coordinator Wang Chonggu received him, reported the matter to court, and asked that an official post be granted to him.

sentences.zh: 朝議多以為不可，拱與居正力主之。

translations.literal: Most at court held that it could not be done; Gong and Juzheng strongly advocated it.
translations.idiomatic: Most at court thought it inadvisable, but Gong and Zhang Juzheng vigorously argued in its favor.

sentences.zh: 遂排眾議請於上，而封貢以成。

translations.literal: He then set aside the collective objections and appealed to the throne, and tribute relations were thereby established.
translations.idiomatic: He overrode the opposition and appealed to the emperor, and tribute relations were successfully established.

sentences.zh: 事具崇古傳。

translations.literal: The matter is fully recorded in Chonggu's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The affair is fully recorded in Wang Chonggu's biography.

sentences.zh: 進拱少師兼太子太師、尚書、大學士，改建極殿。

translations.literal: Gong was promoted to Junior Preceptor with concurrent titles as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister, and Grand Secretary, and assigned to Jianji Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Gong was promoted to Junior Preceptor with concurrent titles as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister, and Grand Secretary, and given the Jianji Hall grand secretaryship.

sentences.zh: 拱以邊境稍寧，恐將士惰玩，復請敕邊臣及時閒暇，嚴為整頓，仍時遣大臣閱視。

translations.literal: Gong, because the border had grown somewhat peaceful, feared that officers and soldiers would grow idle and negligent; he again requested an edict ordering border officials, whenever they had spare time, to reorganize defenses strictly, and still to dispatch grandees periodically to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: Because the frontier had grown somewhat quiet, Gong feared the troops would slacken and grow careless; he again asked that border officials be ordered, in any spare time they had, to tighten discipline and defenses, and that senior ministers be sent from time to time to inspect.

sentences.zh: 帝皆從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all of these proposals.

sentences.zh: 遼東奏捷，進柱國、中極殿大學士。

translations.literal: When Liaodong reported victory, he was promoted to Pillar of State and Grand Secretary of Zhongji Hall.
translations.idiomatic: After Liaodong reported a victory, he was promoted to Pillar of State and Grand Secretary of Zhongji Hall.

sentences.zh: 尋考察科道，拱請與都察院同事。

translations.literal: Soon an evaluation of the censorate and remonstrance officials was conducted; Gong requested to join the Censorate in the work.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, when the censorate and remonstrance officials were being evaluated, Gong asked to take part in the work together with the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 時大學士趙貞吉掌都察院，持議稍異同。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Secretary Zhao Zhenji was in charge of the Censorate, and his views differed somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Grand Secretary Zhao Zhenji was directing the Censorate, and his views differed somewhat from Gong's.

sentences.zh: 給事中韓楫劾貞吉有所私庇。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Han Ji impeached Zhenji for showing partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Han Ji impeached Zhao Zhenji for showing favoritism.

sentences.zh: 貞吉疑拱嗾之，遂抗章劾拱，拱亦疏辨。

translations.literal: Zhenji suspected Gong had incited this and submitted a forceful memorial impeaching Gong; Gong likewise submitted a memorial in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenji suspected Gong had put Han up to it and submitted a forceful memorial impeaching Gong; Gong in turn submitted a memorial defending himself.

sentences.zh: 帝不直貞吉，令致仕去。

translations.literal: The emperor did not support Zhenji and ordered him to retire.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not take Zhenji's side and ordered him to retire from office.

sentences.zh: 拱既逐貞吉，專橫益著。

translations.literal: After Gong had driven Zhenji out, his domineering conduct became even more conspicuous.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gong had driven Zhenji out, his overbearing conduct became even more conspicuous.

sentences.zh: 尚寶卿劉奮庸上疏陰斥之，給事中曹大埜疏劾其不忠十事，皆謫外任。

translations.literal: Court of Imperial Seals Director Liu Fenyong submitted a memorial obliquely rebuking him; Supervising Secretary Cao Daye submitted a memorial impeaching him on ten counts of disloyalty; both were demoted to posts outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Court of Imperial Seals Director Liu Fenyong submitted a memorial that obliquely rebuked him, and Supervising Secretary Cao Daye submitted a memorial impeaching him on ten counts of disloyalty; both were demoted to posts outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 拱初持清操，後其門生、親串頗以賄聞，致物議。

translations.literal: At first Gong maintained an upright reputation, but later his students and relatives were often rumored to take bribes, provoking public criticism.
translations.idiomatic: At first Gong had a reputation for integrity, but later his students and kinsmen were often rumored to accept bribes, provoking public criticism.

sentences.zh: 帝終眷拱不衰也。

translations.literal: The emperor's favor toward Gong remained undiminished to the end.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's favor toward Gong never waned.

sentences.zh: 始拱為祭酒，居正為司業，相友善，拱亟稱居正才。

translations.literal: When Gong first served as Chancellor of the National Academy and Juzheng as Vice Chancellor, they were on friendly terms, and Gong often praised Juzheng's talent.
translations.idiomatic: When Gong first served as chancellor of the National Academy and Juzheng as vice chancellor, they were on friendly terms, and Gong often praised Juzheng's talent.

sentences.zh: 及是李春芳、陳以勤皆去，拱為首輔，居正肩隨之。

translations.literal: By then Li Chunfang and Chen Yiqin had both departed; Gong became chief grand secretary, and Juzheng followed close at his shoulder.
translations.idiomatic: By then Li Chunfang and Chen Yiqin had both left office; Gong became chief grand secretary, and Juzheng followed close behind him.

sentences.zh: 拱性直而傲，同官殷士儋輩不能堪，居正獨退然下之，拱不之察也。

translations.literal: Gong was upright but arrogant by nature; colleagues such as Yin Shidan could not bear him; Juzheng alone deferentially lowered himself, and Gong did not perceive it.
translations.idiomatic: Gong was upright but arrogant by nature; colleagues such as Yin Shidan could not endure him, but Juzheng alone deferentially kept himself below Gong, and Gong did not notice.

sentences.zh: 馮保者，中人，性黠，次當掌司禮監，拱薦陳洪及孟沖，帝從之，保以是怨拱。

translations.literal: Feng Bao was a eunuch, clever by nature; next in line to head the Directorate of Ceremonial. Gong recommended Chen Hong and Meng Chong; the emperor agreed, and for this Bao resented Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Bao was a eunuch, clever by nature, and next in line to head the Directorate of Ceremonial. Gong recommended Chen Hong and Meng Chong instead; the emperor agreed, and Bao resented Gong for it.

sentences.zh: 而居正與保深相結。

translations.literal: Juzheng, meanwhile, was deeply allied with Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng, meanwhile, had formed a deep alliance with Bao.

sentences.zh: 六年春，帝得疾，大漸，召拱與居正、高儀受顧命而崩。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year the emperor fell ill and grew gravely ill; he summoned Gong, Juzheng, and Gao Yi to receive his final charge and then died.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year the emperor fell gravely ill; he summoned Gong, Juzheng, and Gao Yi to receive his deathbed charge, then died.

sentences.zh: 初，帝意專屬閣臣，而中官矯遺詔命與馮保共事。

translations.literal: At first the emperor's intention was to entrust matters solely to the grand secretaries, but the eunuchs forged the testamentary edict to appoint him to serve jointly with Feng Bao.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor had intended to entrust affairs solely to the grand secretaries, but the eunuchs forged the testamentary edict so that Gong was ordered to serve jointly with Feng Bao.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，拱以主上幼沖，懲中官專政，條奏請詘司禮權，還之內閣。

translations.literal: When Shenzong ascended the throne, Gong, because the sovereign was young, and mindful of eunuch domination, submitted a detailed memorial requesting that the Directorate of Ceremonial's power be curtailed and returned to the inner cabinet.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong ascended the throne, Gong, seeing that the emperor was still a child and mindful of eunuch domination, submitted a detailed memorial asking that the Directorate of Ceremonial be stripped of its power and that authority be restored to the inner cabinet.

sentences.zh: 又命給事中雒遒、程文合疏攻保，而己從中擬旨逐之。

translations.literal: He also ordered Supervising Secretaries Luo Qiu and Cheng Wen to submit a joint memorial attacking Bao, while he himself from within would draft an edict to dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Supervising Secretaries Luo Qiu and Cheng Wen to submit a joint memorial attacking Bao, while he himself would draft from within an edict to dismiss him.

sentences.zh: 拱使人報居正，居正陽諾之，而私以語保。

translations.literal: Gong sent word to Juzheng; Juzheng openly agreed, but secretly informed Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Gong sent word to Juzheng; Juzheng agreed openly, but secretly told Bao.

sentences.zh: 保訴於太后，謂拱擅權，不可容。

translations.literal: Bao complained to the empress dowager, saying Gong was grasping power and could not be tolerated.
translations.idiomatic: Bao appealed to the empress dowager, saying Gong was seizing power and could not be tolerated.

sentences.zh: 太后頷之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager nodded in agreement.

sentences.zh: 明日，召群臣入，宣兩宮及帝詔。

translations.literal: The next day the ministers were summoned, and edicts of the two palaces and the emperor were proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the ministers were summoned in, and edicts from the two palaces and the emperor were proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 拱意必逐保也，急趨入。

translations.literal: Gong assumed Bao would surely be expelled and hurried in.
translations.idiomatic: Gong assumed Bao would surely be expelled and hurried in.

sentences.zh: 比宣詔，則數拱罪而逐之。

translations.literal: When the edicts were proclaimed, they enumerated Gong's crimes and expelled him instead.
translations.idiomatic: When the edicts were read, they listed Gong's crimes and expelled him instead.

sentences.zh: 拱伏地不能起，居正掖之出，僦騾車出宣武門。

translations.literal: Gong prostrated himself and could not rise; Juzheng helped him out, and he hired a mule cart and departed through Xuanwu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Gong prostrated himself and could not get up; Juzheng helped him out, and he hired a mule cart and left through Xuanwu Gate.

sentences.zh: 居正乃與儀請留拱，弗許。

translations.literal: Juzheng then joined Yi in asking that Gong be retained; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng then joined Gao Yi in asking that Gong be kept on, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 請得乘傳，許之。

translations.literal: They requested that he be allowed use of the post relay; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: They asked that he be allowed use of the post relay, and this was granted.

sentences.zh: 拱既去，保憾未釋。

translations.literal: After Gong had gone, Bao's resentment was still not appeased.
translations.idiomatic: After Gong had gone, Bao's resentment was still not satisfied.

sentences.zh: 復構王大臣獄，欲連及拱，已而得寢。

translations.literal: He again engineered the Wang Dachen case, hoping to implicate Gong, but in the end the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: He again engineered the Wang Dachen case, hoping to implicate Gong, but in the end the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 居家數年，卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home for several years and died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home for several years, then died.

sentences.zh: 居正請復其官，與祭葬如例。

translations.literal: Juzheng requested restoration of his offices and burial rites according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng asked that his offices be restored and that he be granted the customary sacrificial and burial honors.

sentences.zh: 中旨給半葬，祭文仍寓貶詞雲。

translations.literal: An imperial rescript granted only half the customary burial honors, and the sacrificial text still contained language of reproof.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial rescript granted only half the customary burial honors, and the sacrificial text still contained language of censure.

sentences.zh: 久之，廷議論拱功，贈太師，諡文襄，廕嗣子務觀為尚寶丞。

translations.literal: After some time court discussion assessed Gong's merits; he was posthumously granted the title Grand Preceptor, given the posthumous name Wenxiang, and his heir son Wuguan was granted appointment as Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Seals.
translations.idiomatic: After some time the court reviewed Gong's merits; he was posthumously granted the title Grand Preceptor, given the posthumous name Wenxiang, and his heir son Wuguan was granted appointment as Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Seals.

sentences.zh: 附 郭樸

translations.literal: Appended: Guo Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Guo Pu.

sentences.zh: 郭樸，字質夫，安陽人。

translations.literal: Guo Pu, style Zhifu, was a native of Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu, whose style was Zhifu, came from Anyang.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourteenth year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士。

translations.literal: He was selected as a junior compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as a junior compiler in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 累官禮部右侍郎，入直西苑。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Vice Minister of Rites and entered service at the Western Park.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Vice Minister of Rites and entered service at the Western Park.

sentences.zh: 歷吏部左、右侍郎兼太子賓客。

translations.literal: He successively served as Left and Right Vice Minister of Personnel, concurrently as Preceptor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as Left and Right Vice Minister of Personnel, concurrently as Preceptor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 南京禮部缺尚書，帝憐樸久次，特加太子少保擢任之。

translations.literal: The Nanjing Ministry of Rites lacked a minister; the emperor, pitying Pu's long wait in rank, specially added the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and promoted him to the post.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nanjing Ministry of Rites lacked a minister, the emperor, taking pity on Pu's long wait for promotion, specially added the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and promoted him to the post.

sentences.zh: 樸辭曰：「幸與撰述，不欲遠離闕下。」

translations.literal: Pu declined, saying: "I have the good fortune to assist in compilation and do not wish to leave Your Majesty's presence."
translations.idiomatic: Pu declined, saying, "I have the good fortune to assist in compilation and do not wish to leave Your Majesty's presence."

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，命即以太子少保、禮部尚書、詹事府侍直如故。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and ordered that he be immediately appointed Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Rites, continuing his attendance at the Directorate of the Household of the Heir Apparent as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and ordered that he be immediately appointed Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Rites, while continuing his attendance at the Directorate of the Household of the Heir Apparent as before.

sentences.zh: 頃之，吏部尚書歐陽必進罷，即以樸代之。

translations.literal: Soon after, Minister of Personnel Ouyang Bijin was dismissed and Pu replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Minister of Personnel Ouyang Bijin was dismissed, and Pu replaced him.

sentences.zh: 越二年，以父喪去。

translations.literal: Two years later he left office on his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he left office to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 及嚴訥由吏部入閣，帝謀代者。

translations.literal: When Yan Ne entered the cabinet from the Ministry of Personnel, the emperor sought a replacement.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Ne entered the cabinet from the Ministry of Personnel, the emperor began looking for a replacement.

sentences.zh: 時董份以工部尚書行吏部左侍郎事，方受帝眷，而為人貪狡無行。

translations.literal: At the time Dong Fen, as Minister of Works acting in the duties of Left Vice Minister of Personnel, was enjoying imperial favor, but he was greedy and cunning and without moral conduct.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Dong Fen, as Minister of Works acting in the duties of Left Vice Minister of Personnel, was enjoying imperial favor, but he was greedy, cunning, and utterly without principle.

sentences.zh: 徐階慮其代訥，急言於帝，起樸故官。

translations.literal: Xu Jie, fearing he would replace Ne, urgently spoke to the emperor and had Pu restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jie, fearing that Dong would replace Ne, urgently spoke to the emperor and had Pu restored to his former office.

sentences.zh: 樸固請終制，不許。

translations.literal: Pu firmly requested to complete mourning; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Pu firmly asked to complete his mourning period, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 尋以考績，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Soon on the basis of his performance review he was given the concurrent title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, on the basis of his performance review, he was given the concurrent title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，兼武英殿大學士，入預機務，與高拱並命。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he was concurrently made Grand Secretary of Wuying Hall, entered to participate in state affairs, and appointed together with Gao Gong.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year he was concurrently made Grand Secretary of Wuying Hall, entered to participate in state affairs, and appointed together with Gao Gong.

sentences.zh: 階早貴，權重，春芳、訥事之謹，至不敢講鈞禮。

translations.literal: Jie had risen early and wielded great power; Chunfang and Ne served him respectfully, even daring not to insist on equal ceremonial status.
translations.idiomatic: Jie had risen early and wielded great power; Chunfang and Ne served him with such deference that they did not even dare insist on equal ceremonial standing.

sentences.zh: 而樸與拱鄉里相得，事階稍倨，拱尤負才自恣。

translations.literal: But Pu and Gong, being fellow townsmen, got along well; they were somewhat haughty toward Jie, and Gong especially relied on his talent and acted willfully.
translations.idiomatic: But Pu and Gong, being fellow townsmen, got along well; they were somewhat haughty toward Jie, and Gong especially relied on his talent and acted willfully.

sentences.zh: 及世宗崩，階草遺詔，盡反時政之不便者。

translations.literal: When Shizong died, Jie drafted the testamentary edict, reversing all inconvenient policies.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong died, Jie drafted the testamentary edict, reversing all the policies that had proved inconvenient.

sentences.zh: 拱與樸不得與聞，大恚，兩人遂與階有隙。

translations.literal: Gong and Pu were not permitted to participate; greatly angered, the two thereafter had a breach with Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Gong and Pu were not allowed to take part; greatly angered, the two thereafter fell out with Jie.

sentences.zh: 言路劾拱者多及樸。

translations.literal: Many denunciations of Gong from the remonstrance officers also involved Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the remonstrance officers' attacks on Gong also implicated Pu.

sentences.zh: 拱謝病歸，樸不自安，亦求去。

translations.literal: Gong resigned citing illness; Pu felt uneasy and also sought to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Gong resigned citing illness and returned home; Pu felt uneasy and also asked to leave office.

sentences.zh: 帝固留之。

translations.literal: The emperor firmly kept him on.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor firmly kept him in office.

sentences.zh: 時樸已加至少傅、太子太傅矣。

translations.literal: By then Pu had already been promoted to Junior Tutor and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: By then Pu had already been promoted to Junior Tutor and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 御史龐尚鵬、凌儒等攻不止，遂三疏乞歸。

translations.literal: Censors Pang Shangpeng, Ling Ru, and others pressed their attacks without ceasing; he submitted three memorials requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Pang Shangpeng, Ling Ru, and others kept up their attacks without cease; he submitted three memorials asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 家居二十餘年卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home for more than twenty years and died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home for more than twenty years, then died.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，諡文簡。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Grand Tutor and given the posthumous name Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Grand Tutor and given the posthumous name Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 樸為人長者，兩典銓衡，以廉著。

translations.literal: Pu was by nature a dignified elder; twice he presided over personnel selection and was noted for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was by nature a dignified elder; twice he presided over personnel selection and was known for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 輔政二年無過。

translations.literal: In two years as grand secretary he committed no fault.
translations.idiomatic: In two years as a grand secretary he committed no fault.

sentences.zh: 特以拱故，不容於朝，時頗有惜之者。

translations.literal: Only because of Gong he could not remain at court; many at the time regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Only because of his association with Gong could he not remain at court, and many at the time regretted it.

sentences.zh: 張居正

translations.literal: Zhang Juzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng.

sentences.zh: 張居正，字叔大，江陵人。

translations.literal: Zhang Juzheng, style Shuda, was a native of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng, whose style was Shuda, came from Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 少穎敏絕倫。

translations.literal: From youth he was exceptionally sharp and clever.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was exceptionally quick and clever.

sentences.zh: 十五為諸生。

translations.literal: At fifteen he became a licensed student.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he became a licensed student.

sentences.zh: 巡撫顧璘奇其文，曰：「國器也。」

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Gu Lin was struck by his writing and said: "Material for state service."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Gu Lin was struck by his writing and said, "This is material for state service.

sentences.zh: 未幾，居正舉於鄉，璘解犀帶以贈，且曰：「君異日當腰玉，犀不足溷子。」

translations.literal: Before long Juzheng passed the provincial examination; Gu unfastened his rhinoceros-horn belt and gave it to him, adding: "One day you will wear jade at your waist; rhinoceros horn is not fit to sully you."
translations.idiomatic: Before long Juzheng passed the provincial examination; Gu unfastened his rhinoceros-horn belt and gave it to him, adding, "One day you will wear jade at your waist; rhinoceros horn is not fit to sully you.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十六年，居正成進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing Juzheng passed the jinshi examination and was appointed junior compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing Juzheng passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a junior compiler.

sentences.zh: 日討求國家典故。

translations.literal: Day by day he researched the institutions and precedents of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Day by day he studied the institutions and precedents of the state.

sentences.zh: 徐階輩皆器重之。

translations.literal: Xu Jie and his circle all valued him highly.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jie and his circle all held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 授編修，請急歸，亡何還職。

translations.literal: Appointed compiler, he requested emergency leave to return home, and before long resumed his post.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed compiler, he requested emergency leave to return home, and before long resumed his post.

sentences.zh: 居正為人，頎面秀眉目，須長至腹。

translations.literal: Juzheng in person was long-faced, with handsome eyebrows and eyes, and a beard reaching to his belly.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng was long-faced, with handsome brows and eyes, and a beard that reached to his belly.

sentences.zh: 勇敢任事，豪傑自許。

translations.literal: Bold and willing to take on affairs, he considered himself a man of heroic stature.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and willing to take on affairs, he considered himself a man of heroic stature.

sentences.zh: 然沉深有城府，莫能測也。

translations.literal: Yet he was deep and guarded, and no one could fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was deep and guarded, and no one could fathom him.

sentences.zh: 嚴嵩為首輔，忌階，善階者皆避匿。

translations.literal: Yan Song was chief grand secretary; he envied Jie, and those favorable to Jie all kept out of sight.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song was chief grand secretary; he envied Jie, and those who favored Jie all kept out of sight.

sentences.zh: 居正自如，嵩亦器居正。

translations.literal: Juzheng conducted himself as usual, and Song also appreciated Juzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng conducted himself as usual, and Song also appreciated him.

sentences.zh: 遷右中允，領國子司業事。

translations.literal: Promoted to Right Sub-Reader, he took charge of the vice-chancellorship of the National Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Right Sub-Reader, he took charge of the vice-chancellorship of the National Academy.

sentences.zh: 與祭酒高拱善，相期以相業。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Chancellor Gao Gong and they pledged to each other a career as grand secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: He was on good terms with Chancellor Gao Gong, and they pledged to each other a career as grand secretaries.

sentences.zh: 尋還理坊事，遷侍裕邸講讀。

translations.literal: Soon he returned to Hanlin duties; promoted to serve the Prince of Yu's establishment as lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he returned to Hanlin duties and was promoted to serve the Prince of Yu's establishment as lecturer.

sentences.zh: 王甚賢之，邸中中官亦無不善居正者。

translations.literal: The prince held him in high regard, and among the eunuchs in the prince's household none failed to speak well of Juzheng.
translations.idiomatic: The prince held him in high regard, and among the eunuchs in the prince's household none failed to speak well of Juzheng.

sentences.zh: 而李芳數從問書義，頗及天下事。

translations.literal: Li Fang often came to inquire about the meaning of texts, and the conversation often ranged to affairs under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fang often came to inquire about the meaning of texts, and their talk often ranged to affairs under heaven.

sentences.zh: 尋遷右諭德兼侍讀，進侍講學士，領院事。

translations.literal: Soon promoted to Right Preceptor with concurrent duty as Reader; advanced to Lecturing Academician and head of the academy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Right Preceptor with concurrent duty as Reader, then advanced to Lecturing Academician and head of the academy.

sentences.zh: 階代嵩首輔，傾心委居正。

translations.literal: When Jie succeeded Song as chief grand secretary, he entrusted Juzheng with his full confidence.
translations.idiomatic: When Jie succeeded Song as chief grand secretary, he entrusted Juzheng with his full confidence.

sentences.zh: 世宗崩，階草遺詔，引與共謀。

translations.literal: When Shizong died, Jie drafted the testamentary edict and consulted with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong died, Jie drafted the testamentary edict and consulted with him.

sentences.zh: 尋遷禮部右侍郎兼翰林院學士。

translations.literal: Soon promoted to Vice Minister of Rites with concurrent Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites with concurrent Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 月余，與裕邸故講官陳以勤俱入閤，而居正為吏部左侍郎兼東閣大學士。

translations.literal: After a little more than a month he and Chen Yiqin, formerly lecturers in the Prince of Yu's establishment, both entered the cabinet, while Juzheng became Left Vice Minister of Personnel with concurrent Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a month he and Chen Yiqin, formerly lecturers in the Prince of Yu's establishment, both entered the cabinet, while Juzheng became Left Vice Minister of Personnel with concurrent Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 尋充《世宗實錄》總裁，進禮部尚書兼武英殿大學士，加少保兼太子太保，去學士五品僅歲余。

translations.literal: Soon appointed chief compiler of the Veritable Records of Shizong; promoted to Minister of Rites with concurrent Grand Secretary of Wuying Hall, given the additional titles Junior Guardian with concurrent Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent—a rise of more than five ranks in little over a year since leaving the fifth-rank academician post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed chief compiler of the Veritable Records of Shizong; promoted to Minister of Rites with concurrent Grand Secretary of Wuying Hall, and given the additional titles Junior Guardian with concurrent Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent—advancing more than five ranks in little over a year since leaving his fifth-rank academician post.

sentences.zh: 時徐階以宿老居首輔，與李春芳皆折節禮士。

translations.literal: At the time Xu Jie, an elder statesman, held the chief grand secretaryship, and he and Li Chunfang both humbled themselves to honor scholars.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xu Jie, an elder statesman, held the chief grand secretaryship, and he and Li Chunfang both humbled themselves to honor scholars.

sentences.zh: 居正最後入，獨引相體，倨見九卿，無所延納。

translations.literal: Juzheng entered last, alone adopted the bearing of a chief minister, arrogantly received the Nine Ministers, and did not extend or admit anyone.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng had entered the cabinet last, yet he alone assumed the air of a chief minister—haughtily receiving the Nine Ministers and refusing to solicit or welcome others.

sentences.zh: 間出一語輒中肯，人以是嚴憚之，重於他相。

translations.literal: From time to time he would utter a remark that always hit the mark; people therefore feared him greatly, holding him in greater awe than the other grand secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: When he did speak, a single remark would strike to the heart of the matter; men therefore stood in awe of him, and feared him more than they did the other grand secretaries.

sentences.zh: 高拱以很躁被論去，徐階亦去，春芳為首輔。

translations.literal: Gao Gong was driven out for being very harsh and impetuous; Xu Jie also left; Chunfang became chief grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gong was driven from office for his harsh and impetuous conduct; Xu Jie departed as well, and Li Chunfang became chief grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 亡何，趙貞吉入，易視居正。

translations.literal: Before long Zhao Zhenji entered the cabinet and looked lightly upon Juzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhao Zhenji entered the cabinet and treated Juzheng with open contempt.

sentences.zh: 居正與故所善掌司禮者李芳謀，召用拱，俾領吏部，以扼貞吉，而奪春芳政。

translations.literal: Juzheng plotted with Li Fang, whom he had formerly been on good terms with and who controlled the Directorate of Ceremonial, to recall and employ Gong, have him head the Ministry of Personnel, check Zhenji, and seize Chunfang's power.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng conspired with Li Fang, an old ally who controlled the Directorate of Ceremonial, to recall Gao Gong and put him in charge of the Ministry of Personnel—checking Zhao Zhenji and stripping Li Chunfang of real authority.

sentences.zh: 拱至，益與居正善。

translations.literal: When Gong arrived, he and Juzheng became even closer.
translations.idiomatic: When Gong arrived, he and Juzheng drew even closer.

sentences.zh: 春芳尋引去，以勤亦自引，而貞吉、殷士儋皆為所構罷，獨居正與拱在，兩人益相密。

translations.literal: Chunfang soon resigned; Yiqin also resigned on his own; Zhenji and Yin Shidan were both framed and dismissed; only Juzheng and Gong remained, and the two grew ever closer.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chunfang soon resigned; Chen Yiqin withdrew as well; Zhao Zhenji and Yin Shidan were both framed and driven out. Only Juzheng and Gong remained, and the two grew ever more intimate.

sentences.zh: 拱主封俺答，居正亦贊之，授王崇古等以方略。

translations.literal: Gong advocated enfeoffment of Altan; Juzheng also endorsed it and entrusted Wang Chonggu and others with strategic plans.
translations.idiomatic: Gong advocated enfeoffing Altan Khan; Juzheng endorsed the policy and entrusted Wang Chonggu and others with the strategy.

sentences.zh: 加柱國、太子太傅。

translations.literal: He was given the additional titles Pillar of the State and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the additional titles Pillar of the State and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 六年滿，加少傅、吏部尚書、建極殿大學士。

translations.literal: When six years were complete, he was given Junior Tutor, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of Jianji Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When his six-year term was complete, he was made Junior Tutor, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of Jianji Hall.

sentences.zh: 以遼東戰功，加太子太師。

translations.literal: For military merit in Liaodong, he was given Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: For military merit in Liaodong, he was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 和市成，加少師，余如故。

translations.literal: When the border market was established, he was given Junior Preceptor; other titles remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the border market was established, he was made Junior Preceptor; his other titles remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 初，徐階既去，令三子事居正謹。

translations.literal: At first, after Xu Jie had left, he ordered his three sons to serve Juzheng respectfully.
translations.idiomatic: At first, after Xu Jie had left office, he ordered his three sons to attend on Juzheng with strict deference.

sentences.zh: 而拱銜階甚，嗾言路追論不已，階諸子多坐罪。

translations.literal: But Gong bore a deep grudge against Jie and instigated the censorate and remonstrance officials to pursue and criticize without cease; many of Jie's sons were convicted.
translations.idiomatic: But Gao Gong nursed a deep grudge against Xu Jie and incited the censorate and remonstrance officials to pursue him without letup; many of Jie's sons were convicted.

sentences.zh: 居正從容為拱言，拱稍心動。

translations.literal: Juzheng calmly spoke on Jie's behalf; Gong was somewhat moved.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng spoke calmly on Jie's behalf, and Gong was somewhat moved.

sentences.zh: 而拱客構居正納階子三萬金，拱以誚居正。

translations.literal: But a client of Gong framed Juzheng for accepting thirty thousand taels of gold from Jie's sons; Gong used this to reproach Juzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Then a client of Gong's fabricated a charge that Juzheng had accepted thirty thousand taels of gold from Jie's sons, and Gong used it to rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 居正色變，指天誓，辭甚苦。

translations.literal: Juzheng's face changed color; he pointed to heaven and swore, his words full of anguish.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng's face changed; he pointed to heaven and swore his innocence, his words full of anguish.

sentences.zh: 拱謝不審，兩人交遂離。

translations.literal: Gong apologized for not having verified the matter; the friendship between the two then dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: Gong apologized for not having verified the charge, but the friendship between the two was broken.

sentences.zh: 拱又與居正所善中人馮保郄。

translations.literal: Gong also fell out with Feng Bao, the eunuch whom Juzheng favored.
translations.idiomatic: Gong also fell out with Feng Bao, the eunuch whom Juzheng favored.

sentences.zh: 穆宗不豫，居正與保密處分後事，引保為內助，而拱欲去保。

translations.literal: When Muzong fell ill, Juzheng and Bao secretly arranged affairs after death, bringing Bao in as inner support, while Gong wanted to remove Bao.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong fell ill, Juzheng and Feng Bao secretly made arrangements for what would follow, bringing Bao in as an ally within the palace—while Gong wanted Bao removed.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，保以兩宮詔旨逐拱，事具拱傳，居正遂代拱為首輔。

translations.literal: When Shenzong ascended, Bao used edicts from the two palaces to drive out Gong—the full account is in Gong's biography—and Juzheng then replaced Gong as chief grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong ascended the throne, Feng Bao used edicts from the two palaces to drive Gao Gong out—the full account is in Gong's biography—and Juzheng then replaced him as chief grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 帝御平臺，召居正獎諭之，賜金幣及繡蟒斗牛服。

translations.literal: The emperor went to the terrace, summoned Juzheng and praised him, bestowing gold, silk coins, and an embroidered python robe with fighting-bull insignia.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to the terrace, summoned Juzheng, and praised him, bestowing gold, silk coins, and an embroidered python robe with fighting-bull insignia.

sentences.zh: 自是賜賚無虛日。

translations.literal: From then on gifts and rewards were never absent for a single day.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, gifts and rewards came almost every day.

sentences.zh: 帝虛己委居正，居正亦慨然以天下為己任，中外想望丰采。

translations.literal: The emperor emptied himself and entrusted everything to Juzheng; Juzheng also took up the realm's welfare with resolve; inside and outside the court all looked to him with admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor emptied himself and entrusted all affairs to Juzheng; Juzheng in turn took the welfare of the realm upon himself with resolve, and court and country alike looked to him with admiration.

sentences.zh: 居正勸帝遵守祖宗舊制，不必紛更，至講學、親賢、愛民、節用皆急務。

translations.literal: Juzheng urged the emperor to observe the ancestral institutions without needless changes; he said lecturing on the classics, drawing near to the worthy, cherishing the people, and economizing were all urgent duties.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng urged the emperor to hold to the ancestral institutions and avoid needless change, and told him that lecturing on the classics, drawing near to the worthy, cherishing the people, and practicing thrift were all urgent duties.

sentences.zh: 帝稱善。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 大計廷臣，斥諸不職及附麗拱者。

translations.literal: In the grand assessment of court officials, he expelled those who were incompetent and those who had attached themselves to Gong.
translations.idiomatic: In the grand assessment of court officials, he expelled the incompetent and those who had attached themselves to Gao Gong.

sentences.zh: 復具詔召群臣廷飭之，百僚皆惕息。

translations.literal: He also drafted an edict summoning the officials to the court to admonish them; the hundred officers all trembled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: He also drafted an edict summoning the officials to court for a public admonition, and the whole bureaucracy trembled in fear.

sentences.zh: 帝當尊崇兩宮。

translations.literal: The emperor was to honor the two palaces.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was to honor both empress dowagers.

sentences.zh: 故事，皇后與天子生母並稱皇太后，而徽號有別。

translations.literal: By precedent, the empress and the emperor's biological mother were both called Empress Dowager, but their honorific titles differed.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, the empress and the emperor's biological mother were both styled Empress Dowager, but their honorific titles differed.

sentences.zh: 保欲媚帝生母李貴妃，風居正以並尊。

translations.literal: Bao wished to flatter the emperor's biological mother, Consort Li, and hinted to Juzheng to honor both equally.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Bao wished to flatter the emperor's biological mother, Consort Li, and hinted to Juzheng that both should be honored equally.

sentences.zh: 居正不敢違，議尊皇后曰仁聖皇太后，皇貴妃曰慈聖皇太后，兩宮遂無別。

translations.literal: Juzheng dared not refuse; it was decided to honor the empress as Empress Dowager Rensheng and the imperial consort as Empress Dowager Cisheng; the two palaces thus became undifferentiated.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng dared not refuse; it was decided to honor the empress as Empress Dowager Rensheng and the imperial consort as Empress Dowager Cisheng, and the two palaces were thus made equal.

sentences.zh: 慈聖徙乾清宮，撫視帝，內任保，而大柄悉以委居正。

translations.literal: Cisheng moved to the Palace of Heavenly Purity, cared for the emperor, trusted Bao within, while all major power was entirely entrusted to Juzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Cisheng moved to the Palace of Heavenly Purity to care for the emperor, trusted Feng Bao within the palace, and entrusted all major power to Juzheng.

sentences.zh: 居正為政，以尊主權、課吏職、信賞罰、一號令為主。

translations.literal: Juzheng's governance took as its principles revering imperial authority, demanding officials fulfill their duties, making rewards and punishments credible, and unifying commands.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng governed on four principles: revering imperial authority, holding officials to their duties, making rewards and punishments credible, and unifying commands.

sentences.zh: 雖萬里外，朝下而夕奉行。

translations.literal: Even ten thousand li away, what was ordered in the morning was carried out by evening.
translations.idiomatic: Even ten thousand li away, what was ordered in the morning was carried out by evening.

sentences.zh: 黔國公沐朝弼數犯法，當逮，朝議難之。

translations.literal: Duke of Qian Mu Chaobi repeatedly violated the law and should be arrested; court discussion found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Qian, Mu Chaobi, had repeatedly broken the law and ought to be arrested, but the court hesitated.

sentences.zh: 居正擢用其子，馳使縛之，不敢動。

translations.literal: Juzheng promoted and employed his son, sent a fast courier to bind him, and he did not dare resist.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng promoted Chaobi's son to office and sent a fast courier to bind him; Chaobi did not dare resist.

sentences.zh: 既至，請貸其死，錮之南京。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, he requested sparing his life and confined him in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chaobi arrived at court, Juzheng asked that his life be spared and had him confined in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 氵曹河通，居正以歲賦逾春，發水橫溢，非決則涸，乃採氵曹臣議，督艘卒以孟冬月兌運，及歲初畢發，少罹水患。

translations.literal: The Cao Shenal was open; Juzheng, because annual tribute grain passed spring, when floodwaters swelled and overflowed—either breach or dry up—adopted the proposals of transport officials, supervising boat crews to exchange and transport in the tenth month, completing shipment by the year's start, and suffering less from water disasters.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Canal was open to shipping, but because the annual tribute grain levy extended past spring, when floodwaters surged and overflowed—breaching dikes if not released, drying up if they were—Juzheng adopted the proposals of canal transport officials and supervised boat crews to load and transport grain in the tenth month, completing dispatch by the year's start and suffering far less from flooding.

sentences.zh: 行之久，太倉粟充盈，可支十年。

translations.literal: Practiced for long, Taicang granary grain was full, enough to last ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Maintained over time, the Taicang granaries filled to capacity—enough grain to last ten years.

sentences.zh: 互市饒馬，乃減太僕種馬，而令民以價納，太僕金亦積四百余萬。

translations.literal: Border markets were abundant in horses, so he reduced stud horses of the Court of Imperial Stud and had commoners pay in price instead; the Court of Imperial Stud's funds also accumulated over four million.
translations.idiomatic: Border markets supplied horses in abundance, so he reduced the Court of Imperial Stud's breeding herds and had commoners pay a fee in lieu of stud service; the court's funds eventually accumulated to more than four million taels.

sentences.zh: 又為考成法以責吏治。

translations.literal: He also established the accountability assessment law to hold officials accountable.
translations.idiomatic: He also instituted the accountability assessment law to enforce official discipline.

sentences.zh: 初，部院覆奏行撫按勘者，嘗稽不報。

translations.literal: At first, when ministries and boards submitted memorials for provincial governors and surveillance commissioners to investigate, responses often delayed without report.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when ministries and boards submitted memorials for provincial governors and surveillance commissioners to investigate, replies were often long delayed or never sent at all.

sentences.zh: 居正令以大小緩急為限，誤者抵罪。

translations.literal: Juzheng ordered limits based on magnitude and urgency; those who missed deadlines were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng set deadlines according to the magnitude and urgency of each matter; those who missed them were punished.

sentences.zh: 自是，一切不敢飾非，政體為肅。

translations.literal: From then on none dared conceal faults; government became solemn.
translations.idiomatic: From then on no one dared conceal faults, and the conduct of government grew stern.

sentences.zh: 南京小奄醉辱給事中，言者請究治。

translations.literal: A minor eunuch in Nanjing drunkenly insulted a supervising secretary; memorialists requested investigation and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: A minor eunuch in Nanjing, drunk, insulted a supervising secretary; memorialists called for investigation and punishment.

sentences.zh: 居正謫其尤激者趙參魯於外以悅保，而徐說保裁抑其黨，毋與六部事。

translations.literal: Juzheng banished the most vehement critic Zhao Canlu abroad to please Bao, and gradually persuaded Bao to restrain his faction from meddling in the Six Ministries' affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng banished the most vehement critic, Zhao Canlu, to a post abroad to please Feng Bao, and gradually persuaded Bao to restrain his faction from meddling in the affairs of the Six Ministries.

sentences.zh: 其奉使者，時令緹騎陰詗之。

translations.literal: For those he sent on missions, he would at times have imperial guards secretly spy on them.
translations.idiomatic: For eunuchs sent on missions, he would at times have imperial guards secretly watch them.

sentences.zh: 其黨以是怨居正，而心不附保。

translations.literal: His faction therefore resented Juzheng, yet their hearts did not attach to Bao.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch faction therefore resented Juzheng, yet their loyalty to Feng Bao was not wholehearted.

sentences.zh: 居正以御史在外，往往凌撫臣，痛欲折之。

translations.literal: Juzheng, because censors abroad often overrode provincial officials, greatly wished to break their pride.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng resented that censors abroad often overrode provincial officials, and was determined to break their arrogance.

sentences.zh: 一事小不合，詬責隨下，又敕其長加考察。

translations.literal: On the slightest disagreement in any matter, rebukes and blame followed immediately; he also ordered their superiors to add them to the assessment.
translations.idiomatic: On the slightest disagreement, rebukes and blame followed at once; he also ordered their superiors to mark them down in the official assessment.

sentences.zh: 給事中余懋學請行寬大之政，居正以為風己，削其職。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Yu Maoxue requested lenient government; Juzheng took it as criticism of himself and stripped him of his post.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Yu Maoxue called for a more lenient government; Juzheng took it as a personal attack and stripped him of his post.

sentences.zh: 御史傅應禎繼言之，尤切。

translations.literal: Censor Fu Yingqi followed with the same argument, even more sharply.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Fu Yingqi followed with the same argument, even more sharply.

sentences.zh: 下詔獄，杖戍。

translations.literal: He was sent to the imperial prison, beaten and banished to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to the imperial prison, beaten, and banished to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 給事中徐貞明等群擁入獄，視具橐饘，亦逮謫外。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Xu Zhenming and others crowded into the prison to see him with provisions; they too were arrested and banished abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretaries Xu Zhenming and others crowded into the prison to bring him food; they too were arrested and banished to posts abroad.

sentences.zh: 御史劉台按遼東，誤奏捷。

translations.literal: Censor Liu Tai inspected Liaodong and mistakenly memorialized a false victory.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Liu Tai was inspecting Liaodong when he mistakenly memorialized a false victory.

sentences.zh: 居正方引故事繩督之，台抗章論居正專恣不法，居正怒甚。

translations.literal: Juzheng was just invoking precedent to discipline and supervise him; Tai submitted a defiant memorial accusing Juzheng of arbitrary illegal conduct; Juzheng was very angry.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng was invoking precedent to discipline him when Tai submitted a defiant memorial accusing Juzheng of arbitrary and unlawful conduct; Juzheng was furious.

sentences.zh: 帝為下臺詔獄，命杖百，遠戍。

translations.literal: The emperor had Tai sent to the imperial prison, ordered a hundred strokes, and distant exile.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Tai sent to the imperial prison, ordered him beaten a hundred strokes, and banished him to distant service.

sentences.zh: 居正陽具疏救之，僅奪其職。

translations.literal: Juzheng ostensibly submitted a memorial to save him, requesting only dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng ostensibly submitted a memorial to save him, asking only that he be stripped of his post.

sentences.zh: 已，卒戍台。

translations.literal: Soon after, Tai was ultimately banished to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Tai was banished to frontier service after all.

sentences.zh: 由是諸給事御史益畏居正，而心不平。

translations.literal: From this the supervising secretaries and censors feared Juzheng all the more, yet were inwardly resentful.
translations.idiomatic: From this the supervising secretaries and censors feared Juzheng all the more, yet nursed deeper resentment.

sentences.zh: 當是時，太后以帝沖年，尊禮居正甚至，同列呂調陽莫敢異同。

translations.literal: At this time the empress dowager, because the emperor was young, honored Juzheng to the utmost; his colleague Lü Diaoyang dared not differ.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the empress dowager, because the emperor was still a boy, honored Juzheng to the utmost; his colleague Lü Diaoyang dared not disagree.

sentences.zh: 及吏部左侍郎張四維入，恂恂若屬吏，不敢以僚自處。

translations.literal: When Left Vice Minister of Personnel Zhang Siwei entered the cabinet, he was deferential like a subordinate, not daring to treat himself as an equal colleague.
translations.idiomatic: When Left Vice Minister of Personnel Zhang Siwei entered the cabinet, he was deferential as a subordinate might be, not daring to treat himself as Juzheng's equal.

sentences.zh: 居正喜建豎，能以智數馭下，人多樂為之盡。

translations.literal: Juzheng delighted in establishing achievements, could use schemes to control subordinates; many gladly gave their all for him.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng loved to build his reputation and could use stratagem to control subordinates; many gladly gave their all for him.

sentences.zh: 俺答款塞，久不為害。

translations.literal: Altan submitted at the border and had long ceased to cause harm.
translations.idiomatic: Altan Khan had submitted at the border and had long ceased to threaten the realm.

sentences.zh: 獨小王子部眾十余萬，東北直遼左，以不獲通互市，數入寇。

translations.literal: Only the Little Prince's following of over one hundred thousand, northeast straight toward eastern Liaodong, because they could not obtain border trade, repeatedly raided.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Little Prince, with a following of more than a hundred thousand, pressing northeast toward eastern Liaodong, raided repeatedly because he could not obtain access to the border markets.

sentences.zh: 居正用李成梁鎮遼，戚繼光鎮薊門。

translations.literal: Juzheng employed Li Chenliang to guard Liaodong and Qi Jiguang to guard Jimen.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng put Li Chenliang in command at Liaodong and Qi Jiguang at Jimen.

sentences.zh: 成梁力戰卻敵，功多至封伯，而繼光守備甚設。

translations.literal: Chenliang fought fiercely and repelled the enemy, amassing merit until enfeoffed as earl; Jiguang's defenses were very thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Chenliang fought hard and drove the enemy back, accumulating enough merit to be enfeoffed as an earl; Jiguang's defenses were meticulously prepared.

sentences.zh: 居正皆右之，邊境晏然。

translations.literal: Juzheng favored both; the borders were tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng backed both men, and the borders were tranquil.

sentences.zh: 兩廣督撫殷正茂、凌雲翼等亦數破賊有功。

translations.literal: The governors-general and grand coordinators of the Two Guangs, Yin Zhengmao, Ling Yunyi, and others, also repeatedly defeated bandits with merit.
translations.idiomatic: The governors-general and grand coordinators of the Two Guangs—Yin Zhengmao, Ling Yunyi, and others—also repeatedly defeated bandits with distinction.

sentences.zh: 浙江兵民再作亂，用張佳胤往撫即定，故世稱居正知人。

translations.literal: When Zhejiang soldiers and commoners rebelled again, Zhang Jiayin was sent to pacify and it was immediately settled; therefore the age praised Juzheng for knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: When soldiers and commoners in Zhejiang rebelled again, Juzheng sent Zhang Jiayin to pacify them and the trouble was quickly settled; the age therefore praised Juzheng for knowing how to choose men.

sentences.zh: 然持法嚴。

translations.literal: Yet he held the law strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he enforced the law with rigor.

sentences.zh: 核驛遞，省冗官，清庠序，多所澄汰。

translations.literal: He audited courier stations, reduced redundant officials, cleared the schools, and eliminated many in review.
translations.idiomatic: He audited the courier relay system, cut redundant officials, cleared out the schools, and eliminated many posts in a general review.

sentences.zh: 公卿群吏不得乘傳，與商旅無別。

translations.literal: Grand dukes, ministers, and officials could not ride official relay transport; they were no different from merchants and travelers.
translations.idiomatic: Grand dukes, ministers, and officials could no longer ride the official relay horses; they were treated no differently from merchants and travelers.

sentences.zh: 郎署以缺少，需次者輒不得補。

translations.literal: Because offices lacked vacancies, those awaiting their turn could not be appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Because offices lacked vacancies, those waiting their turn for appointment could not be placed.

sentences.zh: 大邑士子額隘，艱於進取。

translations.literal: In large prefectures examination quotas were narrow; advancement was difficult.
translations.idiomatic: In large prefectures the examination quotas were tight, and advancement was hard.

sentences.zh: 亦多怨之者。

translations.literal: Many also resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Many resented him as well.

sentences.zh: 時承平久，群盜蝟起，至入城市劫府庫，有司恆諱之，居正嚴其禁。

translations.literal: Peace had lasted long; bandits sprang up like hedgehogs, even entering cities to rob treasuries; local officials habitually concealed it; Juzheng strictly forbade concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Peace had lasted so long that bandits sprang up everywhere, even entering cities to loot treasuries; local officials habitually concealed the fact, and Juzheng strictly forbade such cover-ups.

sentences.zh: 匿弗舉者，雖循吏必黜。

translations.literal: Those who concealed and did not report, even diligent officials, were sure to be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Those who concealed crimes and failed to report them were dismissed—even conscientious officials.

sentences.zh: 得盜即斬決，有司莫敢飾情。

translations.literal: When bandits were caught they were immediately executed; officials dared not cover up.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were executed on capture, and officials dared not shield them.

sentences.zh: 盜邊海錢米盈數，例皆斬，然往往長系或瘐死。

translations.literal: Bandits stealing coastal grain and money in full amounts were by rule all executed, yet often they were long imprisoned or died in custody from illness.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits who stole grain or money along the coast in amounts that met the statutory threshold were by rule all executed, yet in practice they were often held for long periods or died in custody from illness.

sentences.zh: 居正獨亟斬之，而追捕其家屬。

translations.literal: Juzheng alone hurried to execute them and pursued their family members.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng alone insisted on swift execution and pursuit of the culprits' families.

sentences.zh: 盜賊為衰止。

translations.literal: Banditry thus declined and ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry accordingly declined.

sentences.zh: 而奉行不便者，相率為怨言，居正不恤也。

translations.literal: But those for whom implementation was inconvenient joined in complaint; Juzheng did not heed it.
translations.idiomatic: Those for whom the new measures were inconvenient joined in complaint, but Juzheng paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 慈聖太后將還慈寧宮，諭居正謂：「我不能視皇帝朝夕，恐不若前者之向學、勤政，有累先帝付托。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Cisheng, about to return to the Palace of Compassion and Tranquility, instructed Juzheng, saying: "I cannot watch over the emperor morning and evening; I fear he will not study and govern as diligently as before, burdening the late emperor's entrustment.
translations.idiomatic: As Empress Dowager Cisheng was about to return to the Palace of Compassion and Tranquility, she instructed Juzheng: "I cannot watch over the emperor morning and evening; I fear he will not study and govern as diligently as before, and so fail the trust the late emperor placed in us.

sentences.zh: 先生有師保之責，與諸臣異。

translations.literal: Sir, you bear the responsibility of tutor and guardian, unlike other ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Sir, you bear the responsibility of tutor and guardian—unlike the other ministers.

sentences.zh: 其為我朝夕納誨，以輔台德，用終先帝憑幾之誼。」

translations.literal: Please day and night instruct him for me, to assist his virtue as ruler, to fulfill the late emperor's trust at his deathbed."
translations.idiomatic: Please instruct him for me day and night, to nurture his virtue as ruler and fulfill the bond the late emperor sealed at his deathbed."

sentences.zh: 因賜坐蟒、白金、彩幣。

translations.literal: She then bestowed a seated python robe, white gold, and colored silks.
translations.idiomatic: She then bestowed on him a python robe for seated wear, white gold, and colored silks.

sentences.zh: 未幾，丁父憂。

translations.literal: Before long, he entered mourning for his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he entered mourning for his father's death.

sentences.zh: 帝遣司禮中官慰問，視粥藥，止哭，絡繹道路，三宮膊贈甚厚。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Directorate of Ceremonial eunuchs to console him, oversee his gruel and medicine, restrain weeping; they thronged the roads; the three palaces sent thick condolence gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent eunuchs from the Directorate of Ceremonial to console him, oversee his gruel and medicine, and restrain excessive weeping; they thronged the roads, and the three palaces sent lavish condolence gifts.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎李幼孜欲媚居正，倡奪情議，居正惑之。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Revenue Li Youzhi wished to flatter Juzheng and initiated the debate on retaining office during mourning; Juzheng was swayed.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Revenue Li Youzhi wished to flatter Juzheng and initiated the debate on retaining office during mourning; Juzheng was swayed.

sentences.zh: 馮保亦固留居正。

translations.literal: Feng Bao also firmly pressed Juzheng to stay.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Bao also pressed hard for Juzheng to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 諸翰林王錫爵、張位、趙志皋、吳中行、趙用賢、習孔教、沈懋學輩皆以為不可，弗聽。

translations.literal: The Hanlin scholars Wang Xijue, Zhang Wei, Zhao Zhigao, Wu Zhongxing, Zhao Yongxian, Xi Kongjiao, Shen Maoxue and others all said it was impermissible; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanlin scholars Wang Xijue, Zhang Wei, Zhao Zhigao, Wu Zhongxing, Zhao Yongxian, Xi Kongjiao, Shen Maoxue, and others all said it was impermissible; he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書張瀚以持慰留旨，被逐去。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Zhang Han, for holding to the edict of consolation retention, was driven out.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Zhang Han, for refusing to endorse the edict urging Juzheng to remain, was driven from office.

sentences.zh: 御史曾士楚、給事中陳三謨等遂交章請留。

translations.literal: Censors Zeng Shichu, supervising secretaries Chen Sanmo and others then submitted successive memorials requesting he stay.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Zeng Shichu, supervising secretaries Chen Sanmo, and others then submitted successive memorials asking that he stay.

sentences.zh: 中行、用賢及員外郎艾穆、主事沈思孝、進士鄒元標相繼爭之。

translations.literal: Zhongxing, Yongxian, Outside Section Director Ai Mu, Section Director Shen Sixiao, and jinshi graduate Zou Yuanbiao successively disputed it.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhongxing, Zhao Yongxian, Outside Section Director Ai Mu, Section Director Shen Sixiao, and jinshi graduate Zou Yuanbiao successively protested.

sentences.zh: 皆坐廷杖，謫斥有差。

translations.literal: All were sentenced to court beating and banishment in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: All were sentenced to beating at court and banishment in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 時彗星從東南方起，長亙天。

translations.literal: At the time a comet rose from the southeast and stretched long across the sky.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a comet rose in the southeast and stretched long across the sky.

sentences.zh: 人情洶洶，指目居正，至懸謗書通衢。

translations.literal: Public feeling was agitated; eyes pointed at Juzheng; slander sheets were even hung in the public thoroughfares.
translations.idiomatic: Public feeling ran high; eyes turned on Juzheng, and slander sheets were even posted in the public streets.

sentences.zh: 帝詔諭群臣，再及者誅無赦，謗乃已。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict instructing the officials: those who touched on it again would be executed without pardon; the slander then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict instructing the officials that anyone who raised the matter again would be executed without pardon; the slander then ceased.

sentences.zh: 於是使居正子編修嗣修與司禮太監魏朝馳傳往代司喪。

translations.literal: Thereupon he dispatched Juzheng's son, Hanlin Compiler S Xiu, together with the Director of Ceremonies eunuch Wei Chao, by relay post to go and take charge of the mourning rites in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent Juzheng's son, Hanlin Compiler S Xiu, and the Director of Ceremonies eunuch Wei Chao by relay post to Jiangling to manage the funeral rites on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 禮部主事曹誥治祭，工部主事徐應聘治喪。

translations.literal: Ministry of Rites Section Director Cao Gao managed the sacrifices; Ministry of Works Section Director Xu Yingpin managed the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry of Rites Section Director Cao Gao oversaw the sacrificial rites, and Ministry of Works Section Director Xu Yingpin oversaw the funeral arrangements.

sentences.zh: 居正請無造朝，以青衣、素服、角帶入閣治政，侍經筵講讀，又請辭歲俸。

translations.literal: Juzheng requested not to attend court, to enter the Grand Secretariat in blue garments, plain white mourning dress, and cornered belt to manage affairs, to attend the Classics Lectern in lecturing and reading, and also requested to decline his annual salary.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng asked to be excused from court audience, to enter the Grand Secretariat in blue garments, plain mourning dress, and a cornered belt to conduct state business, to continue lecturing at the Classics Lectern, and also to forgo his annual stipend.

sentences.zh: 帝許之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted his requests.

sentences.zh: 及帝舉大婚禮，居正吉服從事。

translations.literal: When the emperor performed the grand wedding ceremony, Juzheng participated in auspicious dress.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor celebrated his grand wedding, Juzheng took part wearing festive ceremonial dress.

sentences.zh: 給事中李淶言其非禮，居正怒，出為僉事。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Li Lai said this was improper ritual; Juzheng was angered and had him transferred out as an Assistant Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Li Lai protested that this violated ritual propriety; Juzheng, enraged, had him transferred out to serve as an Assistant Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時帝顧居正益重，常賜居正札，稱「元輔張少師先生」，待以師禮。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor looked upon Juzheng with ever greater regard, often bestowing personal notes on Juzheng, addressing him as "Grand Tutor Zhang, Junior Preceptor, Sir," and treating him with the courtesy due a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor now held Juzheng in ever higher esteem, often sending him personal notes addressed to "Grand Tutor Zhang, Junior Preceptor, Sir," and treating him with the deference owed a teacher.

sentences.zh: 居正乞歸葬父，帝使尚寶少卿鄭欽、錦衣指揮史繼書護歸，期三月，葬畢即上道。

translations.literal: Juzheng begged leave to return and bury his father. The emperor sent Vice Commissioner of the Imperial Insignia Zheng Qin and Embroidered-Uniform Guard Commander Shi Jishu to escort him home, setting a term of three months; after burial was completed he was to take the road back.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng petitioned to return home and bury his father. The emperor sent Vice Commissioner of the Imperial Insignia Zheng Qin and Embroidered-Uniform Guard Commander Shi Jishu to escort him, granting three months' leave and ordering him to resume the journey as soon as the funeral was over.

sentences.zh: 仍命撫按諸臣先期馳賜璽書敦諭。

translations.literal: He further ordered the provincial surveillance and administration officials to dispatch in advance imperial sealed letters of encouragement and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the provincial surveillance and administration officials along the route to send ahead imperial sealed letters of encouragement and instruction.

sentences.zh: 范「帝賚忠良」銀印以賜之，如楊士奇、張孚敬例，得密封言事。

translations.literal: He had cast a silver seal inscribed "The Emperor Rewards the Loyal and Worthy" and bestowed it on him, following the precedents of Yang Shiqi and Zhang Fuyi, granting the privilege of sealed memorials on affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: He had cast for him a silver seal bearing the inscription "The Emperor Rewards the Loyal and Worthy," following the precedents of Yang Shiqi and Zhang Fuyi, and granted him the privilege of submitting sealed memorials on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 戒次輔呂調陽等「有大事毋得專決，馳驛之江陵，聽張先生處分。」

translations.literal: He admonished the Secondary Grand Secretary Lü Diaoyang and others: "On major matters you must not decide alone; dispatch by relay post to Jiangling and leave disposition to Master Zhang."
translations.idiomatic: He instructed Secondary Grand Secretary Lü Diaoyang and the others: "On major affairs you must not decide on your own; send word by relay post to Jiangling and defer to Master Zhang's judgment."

sentences.zh: 居正請廣內閣員，詔即令居正推。

translations.literal: Juzheng requested to expand Grand Secretariat membership; an edict immediately ordered Juzheng to nominate candidates.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng then asked to enlarge the Grand Secretariat, and an edict immediately directed him to submit nominations.

sentences.zh: 居正因推禮部尚書馬自強、吏部右侍郎申時行入閣。

translations.literal: Juzheng thereupon nominated Minister of Rites Ma Ziqiang and Vice Minister of Personnel Shen Shixing for Grand Secretariat appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng accordingly nominated Minister of Rites Ma Ziqiang and Vice Minister of Personnel Shen Shixing for appointment to the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 自強素迕居正，不自意得之，頗德居正，而時行與四維皆自昵於居正，居正乃安意去。

translations.literal: Ziqiang had always been at odds with Juzheng and had not expected to receive the appointment; he was quite grateful to Juzheng. Shixing and Zhang Siwei both maintained close ties with Juzheng on their own account, so Juzheng departed with an easy mind.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ziqiang had long been at odds with Juzheng and never expected the appointment; he was deeply grateful. Shen Shixing and Zhang Siwei both cultivated close ties with Juzheng of their own accord, and so Juzheng left for home with his mind at ease.

sentences.zh: 帝及兩宮賜賚慰諭有加禮，遣司禮太監張宏供張餞郊外，百僚班送。

translations.literal: The emperor and both palaces bestowed gifts and words of consolation with added honors, dispatched Ceremonies eunuch Zhang Hong to provide provisions and a farewell feast outside the city, and the full corps of officials formed ranks to send him off.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and both palaces showered him with gifts and words of consolation befitting his rank, sent Ceremonies eunuch Zhang Hong to provide a farewell feast outside the city, and the entire official corps lined up to see him off.

sentences.zh: 所過地，有司節廚傳，治道路。

translations.literal: Wherever he passed, local officials arranged relay stations and provisions and repaired the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Everywhere he passed, local officials prepared relay stations and provisions and saw to the repair of the roads.

sentences.zh: 遼東奏大捷，帝復歸功居正。

translations.literal: Liaodong reported a great victory; the emperor again attributed the credit to Juzheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Liaodong reported a great victory, the emperor once again credited Juzheng with the achievement.

sentences.zh: 使使馳諭，俾定爵賞。

translations.literal: He sent envoys by relay post to announce the news and directed him to determine ranks and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched envoys by relay post to convey the news and instructed Juzheng to determine the ranks and rewards to be granted.

sentences.zh: 居正為條列以聞。

translations.literal: Juzheng drew up an itemized list and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng drew up an itemized recommendation and submitted it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 調陽益內慚，堅臥，累疏乞休不出。

translations.literal: Diaoyang was all the more ashamed within; he lay abed steadfastly and repeatedly submitted memorials begging retirement, not emerging.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Diaoyang grew ever more ashamed at heart; he took to his bed and repeatedly submitted memorials begging to retire, refusing to come out.

sentences.zh: 居正言母老不能冒炎暑，請俟清涼上道。

translations.literal: Juzheng said his mother was old and could not brave the heat; he asked to wait until it was cool before taking the road.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng said his mother was too old to endure the summer heat and asked to delay his return until the weather turned cool.

sentences.zh: 於是內閣、兩都部院寺卿、給事、御史俱上章，請趣居正亟還朝。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Grand Secretariat, ministers and directors of the Two Capitals' boards, commissions, and courts, supervising secretaries, and censors all submitted memorials urging Juzheng to return to court swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Grand Secretariat, ministers and directors of the Two Capitals' boards, commissions, and courts, supervising secretaries, and censors all submitted memorials urging Juzheng to return to court at once.

sentences.zh: 帝遣錦衣指揮翟汝敬馳傳往迎，計日以俟；

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched Embroidered-Uniform Guard Commander Zhai Rujing by relay post to welcome him, counting the days until his arrival;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Embroidered-Uniform Guard Commander Zhai Rujing by relay post to welcome him home, counting the days until his return;

sentences.zh: 而令中官護太夫人以秋日由水道行。

translations.literal: and ordered eunuchs to escort the Lady Dowager by water route in the autumn.
translations.idiomatic: and ordered eunuchs to escort his mother by water in the autumn.

sentences.zh: 居正所過，守臣率長跪，撫按大吏越界迎送，身為前驅。

translations.literal: Where Juzheng passed, defending officials invariably knelt long; provincial surveillance and administration grand officers crossed their boundaries to welcome and send him off, going ahead in person as outriders.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Juzheng passed, local defending officials invariably knelt in long obeisance; provincial grand officers crossed their jurisdictions to welcome and escort him, riding ahead in person as outriders.

sentences.zh: 道經襄陽，襄王出候，要居正宴。

translations.literal: Passing through Xiangyang, the Prince of Xiang came out to wait for him and pressed Juzheng to a banquet.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Xiangyang, the Prince of Xiang came out to receive him and insisted on hosting a banquet for Juzheng.

sentences.zh: 故事，雖公侯謁王執臣禮，居正具，賓主而出。

translations.literal: By precedent, even dukes and marquises visiting a prince performed the ritual of subjects; Juzheng was fully equipped, and host and guest emerged.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, even dukes and marquises paid obeisance to a prince as subjects; Juzheng appeared in full official regalia, and he and the prince received each other as equals.

sentences.zh: 過南陽，唐王亦如之。

translations.literal: Passing Nanyang, the Prince of Tang did likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Nanyang, the Prince of Tang did the same.

sentences.zh: 抵郊外，詔遣司禮太監何進宴勞，兩宮亦各遣大璫李琦、李用宣諭，賜八寶金釘川扇、御膳、餅果、醪醴，百僚復班迎。
