translations.literal: Upon reaching the suburbs, an edict dispatched Ceremonies eunuch He Jin to feast and comfort him; both palaces also each sent senior eunuchs Li Qi and Li Yong to announce instructions, bestowing eight-treasure gold-studded Sichuan fans, imperial meals, cakes and fruits, and fine liquor; the full corps of officials again formed ranks to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the suburbs of the capital, an edict sent Ceremonies eunuch He Jin to feast and welcome him; both palaces also dispatched senior eunuchs Li Qi and Li Yong with messages of instruction, bestowing eight-treasure gold-studded Sichuan fans, imperial meals, cakes and fruit, and fine liquor, while the full corps of officials again lined up to receive him.

sentences.zh: 入朝，帝慰勞懇篤，予假十日而後入閣，仍賜白金、彩幣、寶鈔、羊酒，因引見兩宮。

translations.literal: Entering court, the emperor consoled and commended him with earnest warmth, granted ten days' leave before re-entering the Grand Secretariat, and again bestowed white silver, brocade silks, treasure notes, mutton and wine, and moreover introduced him to both palaces.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered court, the emperor consoled him with deep warmth, granted ten days' leave before resuming duty in the Grand Secretariat, again bestowed white silver, brocade silks, treasure notes, mutton and wine, and then presented him to both palaces.

sentences.zh: 及秋，魏朝奉居正母行，儀從煊赫，觀者如堵。

translations.literal: When autumn came, Wei Chao escorted Juzheng's mother on the journey; the ceremonial retinue blazed with splendor, and onlookers packed the streets like a wall.
translations.idiomatic: When autumn came, Wei Chao escorted Juzheng's mother on the journey; the ceremonial procession was dazzling in its splendor, and spectators packed the streets wall to wall.

sentences.zh: 比至，帝與兩宮復賜賚加等，慰諭居正母子，幾用家人禮。

translations.literal: By the time they arrived, the emperor and both palaces again bestowed gifts of elevated grade and words of consolation to Juzheng and his mother, almost using the etiquette of family members.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, the emperor and both palaces again bestowed gifts of elevated rank and words of consolation on Juzheng and his mother, treating them almost as members of the imperial household.

sentences.zh: 時帝漸備六宮，太倉銀錢多所宣進。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor was gradually filling the Six Palaces; much silver and coin from the Great Treasury was ordered forwarded to the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was gradually filling the Six Palaces, and large sums of silver and coin from the Great Treasury were being ordered into the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 居正乃因戶部進御覽數目陳之，謂每歲入額不敵所出，請帝置坐隅時省覽，量入為出，罷節浮費。

translations.literal: Juzheng thereupon drew on the figures the Ministry of Revenue submitted for imperial review and memorialized, stating that each year's intake could not match expenditure, and asking the emperor to place the account at his seat corner for frequent review, to match outgo to income, and to abolish and restrain extravagant spending.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng then drew on the revenue figures the Ministry of Revenue submitted for imperial review and memorialized that annual income could not keep pace with expenditure. He asked the emperor to keep the accounts at hand for frequent review, to spend according to income, and to cut back on wasteful expenses.

sentences.zh: 疏上，留中。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and held at court.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and held at court without response.

sentences.zh: 帝復令工部鑄錢給用，居正以利不勝費止之。

translations.literal: The emperor again ordered the Ministry of Works to cast coin for use; Juzheng stopped it on grounds that the profit did not outweigh the cost.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again ordered the Ministry of Works to cast coin for circulation, but Juzheng blocked the plan on the grounds that the costs would outweigh any benefit.

sentences.zh: 言官請停蘇、松織造，不聽。

translations.literal: Censorial officials requested halting Suzhou and Songjiang textile manufacture; [the emperor] would not heed.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials asked that Suzhou and Songjiang textile manufacture be halted, but the emperor would not agree.

sentences.zh: 居正為面請，得損大半。

translations.literal: Juzheng pleaded in person and achieved a reduction of more than half.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng pleaded in person and secured a reduction of more than half.

sentences.zh: 復請停修武英殿工，及裁外戚遷官恩數，帝多曲從之。

translations.literal: He again requested halting repairs on the Hall of Martial Glory and trimming the quota of preferment favors for maternal kin; the emperor largely acquiesced in bent measure.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to halt repairs on the Hall of Martial Glory and to reduce the number of preferments granted to maternal kin; the emperor largely went along.

sentences.zh: 帝御文華殿，居正侍講讀畢，以給事中所上災傷疏聞，因請振。

translations.literal: The emperor held court at the Hall of Literary Glory; when Juzheng had finished attending in lecturing and reading, he reported the disaster and injury memorial submitted by the supervising secretary and thereupon requested relief.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor held audience at the Hall of Literary Glory and Juzheng had finished his lecturing duties, he reported a supervising secretary's memorial on disaster damage and requested relief funds.

sentences.zh: 復言：「上愛民如子，而在外諸司營私背公，剝民罔上，宜痛鉗以法。

translations.literal: He further said: "Your Majesty loves the people as a father loves sons, yet the various offices outside pursue private gain against the public good, stripping the people and deceiving their superiors — they should be sternly restrained by law.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to say: "Your Majesty loves the people as a father loves his children, yet officials in the provinces pursue private gain at public expense, squeezing the people and deceiving the throne. They should be sternly restrained by law.

sentences.zh: 而皇上加意撙節，於宮中一切用度、服御、賞賚、佈施，裁省禁止。」

translations.literal: And Your Majesty should pay added attention to thrift, cutting back and forbidding all palace expenditures, apparel, rewards and grants, and charitable disbursements."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should also pay special heed to thrift, cutting back and forbidding all palace expenditures, apparel, rewards, grants, and charitable disbursements."

sentences.zh: 帝首肯之，有所蠲貸。

translations.literal: The emperor nodded assent and granted some remissions and relief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded assent and granted certain remissions and relief.

sentences.zh: 居正以江南貴豪怙勢及諸奸猾吏民善逋賦，選大吏精悍者嚴行督責。

translations.literal: Juzheng, because Jiangnan's great gentry relied on power and various crafty officials and commoners were adept at evading tax levies, selected tough, capable grand officers to enforce supervision and collection strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jiangnan's great families relied on their power and many crafty officials and commoners were skilled at evading taxes, Juzheng selected tough, capable senior officials to enforce collection strictly.

sentences.zh: 賦以時輸，國藏日益充，而豪猾率怨居正。

translations.literal: Levies were delivered on schedule, the national coffers grew daily fuller, yet the powerful and cunning largely resented Juzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes were delivered on schedule, the national treasury grew steadily fuller, and the powerful and unscrupulous largely came to resent Juzheng.

sentences.zh: 居正服將除，帝召吏部問期日，敕賜白玉帶、大紅坐蟒、盤蟒。

translations.literal: As Juzheng's mourning period was about to end, the emperor summoned the Ministry of Personnel to ask the date, and by edict bestowed a white jade belt, grand red sitting python robes, and coiled python robes.
translations.idiomatic: As Juzheng's mourning period was about to end, the emperor summoned the Ministry of Personnel to inquire about the date and by edict bestowed a white jade belt, grand red sitting-python robes, and coiled-python robes.

sentences.zh: 御平臺召對，慰諭久之。

translations.literal: At the Imperial Platform he summoned Juzheng for audience and consoled and instructed him at length.
translations.idiomatic: At the Imperial Platform the emperor summoned him for audience and consoled and instructed him at length.

sentences.zh: 使中官張宏引見慈慶、慈寧兩宮，皆有恩賚，而慈聖皇太后加賜御膳九品，使宏侍宴。

translations.literal: He had eunuch Zhang Hong introduce him to the Ciqing and Cining palaces; both bestowed favor gifts, and the Empress Dowager Cisheng additionally bestowed a banquet of nine imperial courses, ordering Hong to attend the feast.
translations.idiomatic: He had eunuch Zhang Hong present him to the Ciqing and Cining palaces; both bestowed gifts of favor, and Empress Dowager Cisheng additionally granted a banquet of nine imperial courses and ordered Hong to attend the feast.

sentences.zh: 帝初政，居正嘗纂古治亂事百余條，繪圖，以俗語解之，使帝易曉。

translations.literal: In the early reign, Juzheng once compiled more than a hundred items on order and disorder in antiquity, illustrated them, and explained them in plain language so the emperor could easily understand.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign, Juzheng had compiled more than a hundred episodes of order and disorder from antiquity, illustrated them, and explained them in plain language so the young emperor could easily grasp them.

sentences.zh: 至是，復屬儒臣紀太祖列聖《寶訓》、《寶錄》分類成書，凡四十：曰創業艱難，曰勵精圖治，曰勤學，曰敬天，曰法祖，曰保民，曰謹祭祀，曰崇孝敬，曰端好尚，曰慎起居，曰戒游佚，曰正宮闈，曰教儲貳，曰睦宗籓，曰親賢臣，曰去奸邪，曰納諫，曰理財，曰守法，曰儆戒，曰務實，曰正紀綱，曰審官，曰久任，曰重守令，曰馭近習，曰待外戚，曰重農桑，曰興教化，曰明賞罰，曰信詔令，曰謹名分，曰裁貢獻，曰慎賞賚，曰敦節儉，曰慎刑獄，曰褒功德，曰屏異端，曰節武備，曰御戎狄。

translations.literal: At this point he again charged scholar-officials to compile from the Taizu and successive emperors' Precious Admonitions and Veritable Records, classified into books — forty in all: titled The Hardship of Founding the Enterprise, Exerting Spirit to Govern Well, Diligence in Learning, Reverence for Heaven, Following the Ancestors as Law, Protecting the People, Care in Sacrifices, Honoring Filial Piety and Respect, Uprightness in What One Esteems, Care in Daily Conduct, Warning Against Dissipation, Correcting the Inner Palace, Instructing the Heir Apparent, Harmony with the Imperial Clan and Feudatories, Drawing Near Worthy Ministers, Removing Wicked and Corrupt Men, Accepting Remonstrance, Managing Finances, Upholding the Law, Warning and Admonition, Pursuing What Is Practical, Correcting Institutions and Norms, Examining Officials, Long Tenure in Office, Emphasizing Prefects and Magistrates, Controlling Close Attendants, Treating Maternal Kin, Valuing Agriculture and Sericulture, Promoting Education and Transformation, Clarifying Rewards and Punishments, Trustworthiness of Edicts and Orders, Care in Names and Ranks, Curtailing Tribute Offerings, Care in Bestowal of Rewards, Encouraging Thrift, Care in Penalties and Prisons, Commending Merit and Virtue, Blocking Heterodox Doctrines, Moderating Military Preparations, and Controlling Barbarians of the Frontier.
translations.idiomatic: At this point he again charged scholar-officials to compile selections from the Precious Admonitions and Veritable Records of the Taizu and successive emperors, classified into forty volumes: Founding Hardships, Exerting Oneself to Govern Well, Diligence in Learning, Reverence for Heaven, Following the Ancestors, Protecting the People, Care in Sacrifices, Honoring Filial Piety and Respect, Upright Preferences, Care in Daily Conduct, Warning Against Dissipation, Correcting the Inner Palace, Instructing the Heir Apparent, Harmony with the Imperial Clan and Feudatories, Drawing Near Worthy Ministers, Removing the Wicked and Corrupt, Accepting Remonstrance, Managing Finances, Upholding the Law, Warning and Admonition, Pursuing Practical Results, Correcting Institutions and Norms, Examining Officials, Long Tenure in Office, Emphasizing Prefects and Magistrates, Controlling Close Attendants, Treating Maternal Kin, Valuing Agriculture and Sericulture, Promoting Education and Moral Transformation, Clarifying Rewards and Punishments, Trustworthiness of Edicts and Orders, Care in Names and Ranks, Curtailing Tribute Offerings, Care in Bestowal of Rewards, Encouraging Thrift, Care in Penalties and Prisons, Commending Merit and Virtue, Blocking Heterodox Doctrines, Moderating Military Preparations, and Controlling Frontier Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 其辭多警切，請以經筵之暇進講。

translations.literal: The wording was largely admonitory and urgent; he requested to present and lecture on them during leisure hours at the Classics Lectern.
translations.idiomatic: The language was largely stern and admonitory, and he asked to present and discuss the volumes during intervals at the Classics Lectern.

sentences.zh: 又請立起居注，紀帝言動與朝內外事，日用翰林官四員入直，應制詩文及備顧問。

translations.literal: He also requested establishing Daily Records to chronicle the emperor's words and actions and court internal and external affairs, with four Hanlin officials on daily duty to compose poetry and prose on command and stand ready as advisers.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to establish Daily Records to chronicle the emperor's words and actions and affairs within and beyond the court, with four Hanlin officials on daily duty to compose poetry and prose on command and serve as advisers.

sentences.zh: 帝皆優詔報許。

translations.literal: The emperor in each case replied with gracious edicts granting approval.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied to each request with gracious edicts granting approval.

sentences.zh: 居正自奪情後，益偏恣。

translations.literal: After Juzheng's retention of office during mourning, he became all the more partial and arbitrary.
translations.idiomatic: After Juzheng retained office during mourning against custom, he grew all the more partial and overbearing.

sentences.zh: 其所黜陟，多由愛憎。

translations.literal: His dismissals and promotions largely followed personal likes and dislikes.
translations.idiomatic: His dismissals and promotions were largely driven by personal likes and dislikes.

sentences.zh: 左右用事之人多通賄賂。

translations.literal: Those around him who wielded power largely trafficked in bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Those around him who wielded power were deeply involved in bribery.

sentences.zh: 馮保客徐爵擢用至錦衣衛指揮同知，署南鎮撫。

translations.literal: Feng Bao's client Xu Jue was raised to Embroidered-Uniform Guard Assistant Commander and acted as Southern Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Bao's client Xu Jue was promoted to Assistant Commander of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard and served as acting Southern Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 居正三子皆登上第。

translations.literal: All three of Juzheng's sons passed the highest examinations.
translations.idiomatic: All three of Juzheng's sons passed the highest level of the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 蒼頭游七入貲為官，勛戚文武之臣多與往還，通姻好。

translations.literal: The house servant You Qi purchased office with wealth; many meritorious kin and civil and military officials associated with him and contracted marriage alliances.
translations.idiomatic: His house servant You Qi bought an official post with money, and many meritorious kin and civil and military officials associated with him and formed marriage alliances.

sentences.zh: 七具衣冠報謁，列於士大夫。

translations.literal: Qi, fully dressed in cap and gown, returned calls of visit and took his place among scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: You Qi, dressed in cap and gown, paid return calls of visit and took his place among scholar-officials.

sentences.zh: 世以此益惡之。

translations.literal: The world for this reason hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion for this reason turned against him all the more.

sentences.zh: 亡何，居正病。

translations.literal: Before long Juzheng fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Juzheng fell ill.

sentences.zh: 帝頻頒敕諭問疾，大出金帛為醫藥資。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly issued edicts inquiring after his illness and disbursed great amounts of gold and silk for medical expenses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly issued edicts inquiring after his illness and disbursed large sums of gold and silk for medical expenses.

sentences.zh: 四閱月不愈，百官並齋醮為祈禱。

translations.literal: After four months without recovery, all officials together held abstinent rites and prayers on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: After four months without recovery, officials throughout the court held abstinent rites and prayers on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 南都、秦、晉、楚、豫諸大吏，亡不建醮。

translations.literal: Grand officers of the Southern Capital, Qin, Jin, Chu, Yu, and the rest — none failed to establish prayer altars.
translations.idiomatic: Grand officers of the Southern Capital and the Qin, Jin, Chu, and Yu regions all set up prayer altars without exception.

sentences.zh: 帝令四維等理閣中細務，大事即家令居正平章。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Siwei and others to manage minor affairs in the Secretariat; on major matters they were to have Juzheng at home decide and report.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Zhang Siwei and the others to handle minor affairs in the Grand Secretariat, while major matters were to be decided at home by Juzheng.

sentences.zh: 居正始自力，後憊甚不能遍閱，然尚不使四維等參之。

translations.literal: Juzheng at first exerted himself; later he was so exhausted he could not review everything, yet he still did not allow Siwei and others to participate.
translations.idiomatic: At first Juzheng forced himself to keep working; later he was so exhausted he could not review everything, yet he still would not let Siwei and the others take part.

sentences.zh: 及病革，乞歸。

translations.literal: When his illness reached crisis, he begged to retire home.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness reached crisis, he begged to retire home.

sentences.zh: 上復優詔慰留，稱「太師張太岳先生」。

translations.literal: The emperor again replied with a gracious edict consoling him and urging him to stay, addressing him as "Grand Preceptor Master Zhang Taiyue."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again replied with a gracious edict consoling him and urging him to remain, addressing him as "Grand Preceptor Master Zhang Taiyue."

sentences.zh: 居正度不起，薦前禮部尚書潘晟及尚書梁夢龍、侍郎余有丁、許國、陳經邦，已，復薦尚書徐學謨、曾省吾、張學顏、侍郎王篆等可大用。

translations.literal: Juzheng judged he would not recover and recommended former Minister of Rites Pan Sheng, Ministers Liang Menglong, Vice Ministers Yu Youding, Xu Guo, and Chen Jingbang; afterward he again recommended Ministers Xu Xuemo, Zeng Shengwu, and Zhang Xueyan, Vice Minister Wang Zhuan, and others as fit for great employment.
translations.idiomatic: Believing he would not recover, Juzheng recommended former Minister of Rites Pan Sheng, Minister Liang Menglong, and Vice Ministers Yu Youding, Xu Guo, and Chen Jingbang; he then also recommended Ministers Xu Xuemo, Zeng Shengwu, and Zhang Xueyan, Vice Minister Wang Zhuan, and others as men of great talent.

sentences.zh: 帝為黏御屏。

translations.literal: The emperor had them pasted on the imperial screen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had the names pasted on the imperial screen.

sentences.zh: 晟，馮保所受書者也，強居正薦之。

translations.literal: Sheng was one to whom Feng Bao had owed a favor; he compelled Juzheng to recommend him.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Sheng was a man to whom Feng Bao owed a debt of gratitude, and Feng Bao had pressured Juzheng into recommending him.

sentences.zh: 時居正已昏甚，不能自主矣。

translations.literal: By then Juzheng was already deeply confused and could no longer decide for himself.
translations.idiomatic: By then Juzheng was already deeply confused and could no longer decide for himself.

sentences.zh: 及卒，帝為輟朝，諭祭九壇，視國公兼師傅者。

translations.literal: When he died, the emperor suspended court, ordered sacrifices at nine altars, treating him as a state duke who also served as tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the emperor suspended court and ordered sacrifices at nine altars, treating him as a state duke who had also served as imperial tutor.

sentences.zh: 居正先以六載滿，加特進中極殿大學士；

translations.literal: Juzheng, upon completing six years in office, was specially promoted to Grand Secretary of the Hall of Central Supremacy;
translations.idiomatic: After six years in office, Juzheng had been specially promoted to Grand Secretary of the Hall of Central Supremacy;

sentences.zh: 以九載滿，加賜坐蟒衣，進左柱國，廕一子尚寶丞；

translations.literal: upon completing nine years, was additionally granted sitting python robes, advanced to Left Pillar of the State, and one son was ennobled as Vice Commissioner of the Imperial Insignia;
translations.idiomatic: after nine years he had been granted sitting-python robes, advanced to Left Pillar of the State, and had one son ennobled as Vice Commissioner of the Imperial Insignia;

sentences.zh: 以大婚，加歲祿百石，錄子錦衣千戶為指揮僉事；

translations.literal: on account of the grand wedding, his annual stipend was increased by one hundred shi, and his son, a thousand-household Embroidered-Uniform Guard officer, was enrolled as Assistant Commander;
translations.idiomatic: on account of the grand wedding his annual stipend had been increased by one hundred shi, and his son, a thousand-household Embroidered-Uniform Guard officer, had been enrolled as Assistant Commander;

sentences.zh: 以十二載滿，加太傅；

translations.literal: upon completing twelve years, he was made Grand Tutor;
translations.idiomatic: after twelve years he had been made Grand Tutor;

sentences.zh: 以遼東大捷，進太師，益歲祿二百石，子由指揮僉事進同知。

translations.literal: on account of the great Liaodong victory, he was advanced to Grand Preceptor, his annual stipend was increased by two hundred shi, and his son was promoted from Assistant Commander to Vice Commander.
translations.idiomatic: after the great Liaodong victory he had been advanced to Grand Preceptor, his annual stipend increased by two hundred shi, and his son promoted from Assistant Commander to Vice Commander.

sentences.zh: 至是，贈上柱國，諡文忠，命四品京卿、錦衣堂上官、司禮太監護喪歸葬。

translations.literal: At this point he was posthumously enfeoffed as Upper Pillar of the State, given the posthumous name Wenzhong, and four-rank capital directors, senior Embroidered-Uniform Guard officers, and Ceremonies eunuchs were ordered to escort the funeral home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Now he was posthumously enfeoffed as Upper Pillar of the State, given the posthumous name Wenzhong, and four-rank capital directors, senior Embroidered-Uniform Guard officers, and Ceremonies eunuchs were ordered to escort the funeral home for burial.

sentences.zh: 於是四維始為政，而與居正所薦引王篆、曾省吾等交惡。

translations.literal: Thereupon Siwei at last took charge of government, and he came into bitter conflict with Wang Zhuan, Zeng Shengwu, and others whom Juzheng had promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Zhang Siwei at last took charge of government, and he fell into bitter conflict with Wang Zhuan, Zeng Shengwu, and others whom Juzheng had promoted.

sentences.zh: 初，帝所幸中官張誠見惡馮保，斥於外，帝使密詗保及居正。

translations.literal: Earlier, the eunuch Zhang Cheng whom the emperor favored had been hated by Feng Bao and expelled to the outside; the emperor had him secretly spy on Bao and Juzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the eunuch Zhang Cheng, whom the emperor favored, had been hated by Feng Bao and expelled from court; the emperor had him secretly investigate Feng Bao and Juzheng.

sentences.zh: 至是，誠復入，悉以兩人交結恣橫狀聞，且謂其寶藏逾天府。

translations.literal: At this point Cheng re-entered and fully reported on the two men's collusion and reckless arrogance, moreover saying their treasure stores exceeded the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Zhang Cheng returned to court and fully reported on the two men's collusion and reckless arrogance, adding that their treasure stores exceeded those of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 帝心動。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was moved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was shaken.

sentences.zh: 左右亦浸言保過惡，而四維門人御史李植極論徐爵與保挾詐通姦諸罪。

translations.literal: Those around him also gradually spoke of Bao's transgressions and faults, while Siwei's protégé, Censor Li Zhi, argued at length the crimes of Xu Jue and Bao in wielding fraud and committing adultery together.
translations.idiomatic: Those around the emperor also gradually denounced Feng Bao's misdeeds, while Zhang Siwei's protégé, Censor Li Zhi, argued at length that Xu Jue and Feng Bao had committed fraud, adultery, and other crimes.

sentences.zh: 帝執保禁中，逮爵詔獄。

translations.literal: The emperor seized Bao and confined him within the palace; Xu Jue was arrested and sent to the edict prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor seized Feng Bao and confined him within the palace, and Xu Jue was arrested and sent to the edict prison.

sentences.zh: 謫保奉御居南京，盡籍其家金銀珠寶巨萬計。

translations.literal: Bao was demoted to palace attendant and assigned to Nanjing; the gold, silver, pearls, and jewels of his household were fully inventoried, amounting to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Bao was demoted to palace attendant and sent to Nanjing, and the gold, silver, pearls, and jewels of his household were fully inventoried, amounting to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 帝疑居正多蓄，益心艷之。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected Juzheng had amassed much wealth and was all the more covetous in mind.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected that Juzheng too had amassed great wealth, and his mind turned all the more to coveting it.

sentences.zh: 言官劾篆、省吾，並劾居正，篆、省吾俱得罪。

translations.literal: Censorial officials impeached Zhuan and Shengwu, and also impeached Juzheng; Zhuan and Shengwu both suffered punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials impeached Wang Zhuan and Zeng Shengwu, and also impeached Juzheng; Zhuan and Shengwu both suffered punishment.

sentences.zh: 新進者益務攻居正。

translations.literal: New arrivals all the more devoted themselves to attacking Juzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Newly arrived officials devoted themselves all the more to attacking Juzheng.

sentences.zh: 詔奪上柱國、太師，再奪諡。

translations.literal: An edict stripped the posthumous enfeoffment as Upper Pillar of the State and Grand Preceptor, and again stripped the posthumous name.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped his posthumous enfeoffment as Upper Pillar of the State and Grand Preceptor, and again stripped his posthumous name.

sentences.zh: 居正諸所引用者，斥削殆盡。

translations.literal: Those Juzheng had brought into office were dismissed and demoted almost entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly all of those Juzheng had brought into office were dismissed and demoted.

sentences.zh: 召還中行、用賢等，遷官有差。

translations.literal: Wu Zhongxing, Zhao Yongxian, and others were recalled and promoted in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhongxing, Zhao Yongxian, and others were recalled and promoted in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 劉台贈官，還其產。

translations.literal: Liu Tai was posthumously awarded office and his property restored.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tai was posthumously awarded office, and his property was restored.

sentences.zh: 御史羊可立復追論居正罪，指居正構遼庶人憲節獄。

translations.literal: Censor Yang Keli again pursued charges against Juzheng, accusing him of fabricating the treason case against the Liaodong commoner Xianjie.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yang Keli again pursued charges against Juzheng, accusing him of fabricating the treason case against the deposed Liaodong heir Xianjie.

sentences.zh: 庶人妃因上疏辯冤，且曰：「庶人金寶萬計，悉入居正。」

translations.literal: The deposed heir's consort thereupon submitted a memorial pleading innocence, and furthermore said: "The deposed heir's gold and treasure numbered in the tens of thousands — all of it went to Juzheng."
translations.idiomatic: The deposed heir's consort thereupon submitted a memorial pleading her innocence, and furthermore said: "The deposed heir's gold and treasure numbered in the tens of thousands — all of it went to Juzheng."

sentences.zh: 帝命司禮張誠及侍郎丘橓偕錦衣指揮、給事中籍居正家。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Ceremonies Director Zhang Cheng together with Vice Minister Qiu Yun, an Embroidered-Uniform Guard commander, and a supervising secretary to inventory Juzheng's household.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Ceremonies Director Zhang Cheng, Vice Minister Qiu Yun, an Embroidered-Uniform Guard commander, and a supervising secretary to inventory Juzheng's household.

sentences.zh: 誠等將至，荊州守令先期錄人口，錮其門，子女多遁避空室中。

translations.literal: As Cheng and the others were about to arrive, the prefectural and county magistrates of Jingzhou beforehand recorded the household register and bolted the gates; sons and daughters mostly fled and hid in empty rooms.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhang Cheng and the others were about to arrive, the prefectural and county magistrates of Jingzhou beforehand recorded the household register and bolted the gates; Juzheng's sons and daughters mostly fled and hid in empty rooms.

sentences.zh: 比門啟，餓死者十余輩。

translations.literal: By the time the gate was opened, more than ten persons had died of starvation.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the gate was opened, more than ten people inside had died of starvation.

sentences.zh: 誠等盡發其諸子兄弟藏，得黃金萬兩，白金十余萬兩。

translations.literal: Cheng and the others fully opened the stores of his sons and brothers and obtained ten thousand taels of gold and more than one hundred thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cheng and the others fully opened the stores of Juzheng's sons and brothers and found ten thousand taels of gold and more than one hundred thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 其長子禮部主事敬修不勝刑，自誣服寄三十萬金於省吾、篆及傅作舟等，尋自縊死。

translations.literal: His eldest son, Ministry of Rites Section Director Jingxiu, unable to bear torture, falsely confessed of his own accord that he had sent three hundred thousand taels of gold to Shengwu, Zhuan, and Fu Zuozhou and others; shortly afterward he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son, Ministry of Rites Section Director Jingxiu, unable to bear the torture, falsely confessed of his own accord that he had sent three hundred thousand taels of gold to Zeng Shengwu, Wang Zhuan, Fu Zuozhou, and others; shortly afterward he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 事聞，時行等與六卿大臣合疏，請少緩之；

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Shixing and others together with the six-minister grand secretaries submitted a joint memorial requesting that matters be slightly eased;
translations.idiomatic: When news of the matter reached court, Shen Shixing and others joined the six-minister grand secretaries in a joint memorial asking that the investigation be slightly eased;

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書潘季馴疏尤激楚。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Pan Jixun's memorial was especially pointed and cutting.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Pan Jixun's memorial was especially sharp and uncompromising.

sentences.zh: 詔留空宅一所、田十頃，贍其母。

translations.literal: An edict granted one vacant residence and ten qing of fields to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted one vacant residence and ten qing of land to support Jingxiu's mother.

sentences.zh: 而御史丁此呂復追論科場事，謂高啟愚以舜、禹命題，為居正策禪受。

translations.literal: Then Censor Ding Cilu again pursued the examination-field affair, claiming Gao Qiyu's choice of Shun and Yu as essay topics was Juzheng's scheme for the abdication and succession ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Censor Ding Cilu again pursued the examination scandal, alleging that Gao Qiyu's essay topics on Shun and Yu were a design by Juzheng to arrange abdication and succession.

sentences.zh: 尚書楊巍等與相駁。

translations.literal: Ministers Yang Wei and others rebutted him one by one.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers Yang Wei and others rebutted these claims in turn.

sentences.zh: 此呂出外，啟愚削籍。

translations.literal: Cilu was sent out of office; Qiyu was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Cilu was dismissed from office, and Gao Qiyu was struck from the register.

sentences.zh: 後言者復攻居正不已。

translations.literal: Afterward memorialists again attacked Juzheng without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward critics again attacked Juzheng without letup.

sentences.zh: 詔盡削居正官秩，奪前所賜璽書、四代誥命，以罪狀示天下，謂當剖棺戮死而姑免之。

translations.literal: An edict fully stripped Juzheng of all official rank, confiscated the previously granted seal letters and four generations of patent letters, and displayed his criminal charges to the realm, saying that he ought to have his coffin opened and corpse mutilated but was for the moment spared.
translations.idiomatic: An edict fully stripped Juzheng of all official rank, confiscated the seal letters and patent letters of enfeoffment previously granted to four generations of his family, and published his crimes to the realm, declaring that he deserved to have his coffin opened and corpse executed but was for the moment spared.

sentences.zh: 其弟都指揮居易、子編修嗣修，俱發戍煙瘴地。

translations.literal: His younger brother, Commander Yijian, and his son, Hanlin compiler Sizheng, were both sent into exile in miasmic lands.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother, the commander Yijian, and his son, Hanlin compiler Sizheng, were both banished to miasmic frontier regions.

sentences.zh: 終萬曆世，無敢白居正者。

translations.literal: Throughout the Wanli reign none dared speak on Juzheng's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the remainder of the Wanli reign, no one dared speak up on Juzheng's behalf.

sentences.zh: 熹宗時，廷臣稍稍追述之。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xizong, court officials gradually began to recall his merits.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xizong, court officials gradually began to speak of him again.

sentences.zh: 而鄒元標為都御史，亦稱居正。

translations.literal: When Zou Yuanbiao served as censor-in-chief, he too praised Juzheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Zou Yuanbiao served as censor-in-chief, he too spoke in praise of Juzheng.

sentences.zh: 詔復故官，予葬祭。

translations.literal: An edict restored his former offices and granted funeral sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored his former offices and granted him funeral and sacrificial honors.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年，禮部侍郎羅喻義等訟居正冤。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongzhen, Vice Minister of Rites Luo Yuyi and others petitioned that Juzheng had been wronged.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chongzhen, Vice Minister of Rites Luo Yuyi and others petitioned that Juzheng had been unjustly condemned.

sentences.zh: 帝令部議，復二廕及誥命。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the ministry to deliberate and restored two hereditary privileges and the patent letters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the ministry to deliberate and restored two hereditary privilege appointments and the patent letters of enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 十三年，敬修孫同敞請復武廕，並復敬修官。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Jingxiu's grandson Tongchang requested restoration of the military hereditary privilege and also restoration of Jingxiu's office.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, Jingxiu's grandson Tongchang requested restoration of the military hereditary privilege and the restoration of Jingxiu's office as well.

sentences.zh: 帝授同敞中書舍人，而下部議敬修事。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Tongchang secretary in the Secretariat and referred Jingxiu's case to the ministry for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Tongchang secretary in the Secretariat and referred Jingxiu's case to the ministry for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 尚書李日宣等言：「故輔居正，受遺輔政，事皇祖者十年，肩勞任怨，舉廢飭弛，弼成萬曆初年之治。

translations.literal: Minister Li Rixuan and others stated: "The late Grand Secretary Juzheng received the deathbed charge and assisted in government, serving Our Grandfather for ten years, shouldering toil and accepting blame, raising what was abandoned and tightening what was slack, and helping bring about the good order of the early Wanli years.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Li Rixuan and others stated: "The late Grand Secretary Juzheng received the deathbed charge and assisted in government, serving Our Grandfather for ten years, shouldering toil and accepting blame, raising what was abandoned and tightening what was slack, and helping bring about the good order of the early Wanli years.

sentences.zh: 其時中外乂安，海內殷阜，紀綱法度，莫不修明。

translations.literal: At that time within and without were at peace, the realm within the seas was prosperous, and laws and institutions were none that were not well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the empire was peaceful at home and abroad, prosperously abundant throughout the land, and every law and institution was brought into good order.

sentences.zh: 功在社稷，日久論定，人益追思。」

translations.literal: His merit lay in the altars of state; as time passed judgment settled, and people ever more looked back in remembrance."
translations.idiomatic: His merit lay with the altars of state; as time passed and judgment settled, people remembered him all the more."

sentences.zh: 帝可其奏，復敬修官。

translations.literal: The emperor approved their memorial and restored Jingxiu's office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the memorial and restored Jingxiu's office.

sentences.zh: 曾孫 同敞

translations.literal: Great-grandson: Tongchang
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandson: Tongchang

sentences.zh: 同敞負志節，感帝恩，益自奮。

translations.literal: Tongchang possessed lofty integrity; moved by the emperor's grace, he strove all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Tongchang possessed lofty integrity; moved by the emperor's kindness, he strove all the more.

sentences.zh: 十五年，奉敕慰問湖廣諸王，因令調兵雲南。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, by imperial order he went to convey condolences to the princes of Huguang and was also ordered to mobilize troops in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, by imperial order he went to convey condolences to the princes of Huguang and was moreover ordered to mobilize troops in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 未覆命，兩京相繼失，走詣福建。

translations.literal: Before he reported back, both capitals fell in succession; he fled to Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could report back, both capitals fell in succession, and he fled to Fujian.

sentences.zh: 唐王亦念居正功，復其錦衣世廕，授同敞指揮僉事。

translations.literal: The Prince of Tang also remembered Juzheng's merits, restored his Embroidered-Uniform Guard hereditary privilege, and appointed Tongchang vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Tang also remembered Juzheng's service, restored the family's Embroidered-Uniform Guard hereditary privilege, and appointed Tongchang vice commander.

sentences.zh: 尋奉使湖南。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was sent on mission to Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was sent on mission to Hunan.

sentences.zh: 聞汀州破，依何騰蛟於武岡。

translations.literal: When he heard Tingzhou had fallen, he joined He Tengjiao at Wugang.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Tingzhou had fallen, he joined He Tengjiao at Wugang.

sentences.zh: 永明王用廷臣薦，改授同敞侍讀學士。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yongming, on court recommendation, changed Tongchang's appointment to Reader-in-Waiting in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At court recommendation, the Prince of Yongming changed Tongchang's appointment to Reader-in-Waiting in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 為總兵官劉承胤所惡，言翰林、吏部、督學必用甲科，乃改同敞尚寶卿。

translations.literal: Hated by regional commander Liu Chengyin, who said the Hanlin, Ministry of Personnel, and education commissioners must be filled from jinshi graduates, Tongchang was then changed to Minister of the Court of Imperial Entry.
translations.idiomatic: Disliked by regional commander Liu Chengyin, who argued that the Hanlin Academy, Ministry of Personnel, and education commissioners must be filled from jinshi graduates, Tongchang was then reassigned as Minister of the Court of Imperial Entry.

sentences.zh: 以大學士瞿式耜薦，擢兵部右侍郎兼翰林侍讀學士，總督諸路軍務。

translations.literal: On Grand Secretary Qu Shisi's recommendation, he was promoted to Vice Minister of War and concurrent Reader-in-Waiting in the Hanlin Academy, with overall command of military affairs on all routes.
translations.idiomatic: On Grand Secretary Qu Shisi's recommendation, he was promoted to Vice Minister of War and concurrent Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting, with overall command of military affairs on all routes.

sentences.zh: 同敞有文武材，意氣慷慨。

translations.literal: Tongchang had both civil and military talent, and his spirit was bold and generous.
translations.idiomatic: Tongchang had both civil and military talent, and his spirit was bold and generous.

sentences.zh: 每出師，輒躍馬為諸將先。

translations.literal: Whenever he went out on campaign, he would leap on his horse and take the lead among the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he took the field, he would leap on his horse and lead all the other generals.

sentences.zh: 或敗奔，同敞危坐不去，諸將復還戰，或取勝。

translations.literal: When forces broke and fled, Tongchang would sit upright without leaving; the generals would return to fight again, and sometimes gained victory.
translations.idiomatic: When his troops broke and fled, Tongchang would sit upright without moving; the generals would return to the fight, and sometimes they won.

sentences.zh: 軍中以是服同敞。

translations.literal: Because of this the army came to respect Tongchang.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this the army came to respect Tongchang.

sentences.zh: 大將王永祚等久圍永州，大兵赴救，胡一青率眾迎敵，戰敗。

translations.literal: The great general Wang Yongzuo and others had long besieged Yongzhou; the great army came to the rescue; Hu Yiqing led troops to meet the enemy and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: General Wang Yongzuo and others had long besieged Yongzhou; Qing relief forces arrived; Hu Yiqing led troops to meet them and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 同敞馳至全州，檄楊國棟兵策應，乃解去。

translations.literal: Tongchang galloped to Quanzhou, issued orders for Yang Guodong's troops to coordinate support, and then the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Tongchang galloped to Quanzhou, ordered Yang Guodong's troops to coordinate support from the flank, and the siege was then lifted.

sentences.zh: 順治七年，大兵破嚴關，諸將盡棄桂林走。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Shunzhi, the great army broke through Yanguan; all the generals abandoned Guilin and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Shunzhi, the Qing army broke through Yanguan Pass; the generals all abandoned Guilin and fled.

sentences.zh: 城中虛無人，獨式耜端坐府中。

translations.literal: The city was nearly empty of people; Shisi alone sat upright in the prefectural yamen.
translations.idiomatic: The city was nearly empty; Shisi alone sat upright in the prefectural yamen.

sentences.zh: 適同敞自靈川至，見式耜。

translations.literal: Just then Tongchang arrived from Lingchuan and went to see Shisi.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Tongchang arrived from Lingchuan and went to see Shisi.

sentences.zh: 式耜曰：「我為留守，當死此。

translations.literal: Shisi said: "I am the garrison commissioner; I ought to die here.
translations.idiomatic: Shisi said: "I am the garrison commissioner; I ought to die here.

sentences.zh: 子無城守責，盍去諸？」

translations.literal: You bear no responsibility for defending the city — why not leave?"
translations.idiomatic: You bear no responsibility for holding the city — why not go?"

sentences.zh: 同敞正色曰：「昔人恥獨為君子，公顧不許同敞共死乎？」

translations.literal: Tongchang said sternly: "The ancients were ashamed to be the sole gentleman — will you, sir, not permit Tongchang to die with you?"
translations.idiomatic: Tongchang said sternly: "The ancients were ashamed to stand alone as the gentleman — will you, sir, not allow Tongchang to die with you?"

sentences.zh: 式耜喜，取酒與飲，明燭達旦。

translations.literal: Shisi was pleased; he brought wine and they drank together, with bright candles burning until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Shisi was delighted; he brought wine for them to drink, and they talked by bright candlelight until dawn.

sentences.zh: 侵晨被執，諭之降，不從。

translations.literal: At daybreak they were seized; they were urged to surrender and refused.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak they were seized; urged to surrender, they refused.

sentences.zh: 令為僧，亦不從。

translations.literal: Ordered to become monks, they again refused.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to become monks, they again refused.

sentences.zh: 乃幽之民舍。

translations.literal: They were then confined in a commoner's dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: They were then confined in a commoner's dwelling.

sentences.zh: 雖異室，聲息相聞，兩人日賦詩倡和。

translations.literal: Though in separate rooms, they could hear each other's breathing; the two composed poems daily in mutual response.
translations.idiomatic: Though they were in separate rooms, they could hear each other's breathing; every day the two composed poems in reply to each other.

sentences.zh: 閱四十余日，整衣冠就刃，顏色不變。

translations.literal: After more than forty days, they straightened their robes and caps and went to the blade; their countenances did not change.
translations.idiomatic: After more than forty days, they straightened their robes and caps and went to meet the blade; their expressions did not change.

sentences.zh: 既死，同敞屍植立，首墜躍而前者三，人皆辟易。

translations.literal: After death, Tongchang's corpse stood upright; his head fell and then leaped forward three times, and all shrank back in fear.
translations.idiomatic: After his death, Tongchang's corpse stood upright; his head fell, then leaped forward three times — and everyone shrank back in fear.

sentences.zh: 而居正第五子允修，字建初，廕尚寶丞。

translations.literal: As for Juzheng's fifth son Yunxiu, whose style was Jianchu, he inherited appointment as vice director of the Court of Imperial Regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng's fifth son Yunxiu, whose style was Jianchu, held a hereditary appointment as vice director of the Court of Imperial Regalia.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十七年正月，張獻忠掠荊州，允修題詩於壁，不食而死。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventeenth year of Chongzhen, Zhang Xianzhong plundered Jingzhou; Yunxiu inscribed a poem on the wall and died by fasting.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventeenth year of Chongzhen, Zhang Xianzhong plundered Jingzhou; Yunxiu wrote a poem on the wall and starved himself to death.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：徐階以恭勤結主知，器量深沉。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Xu Jie, through reverence and diligence, won the ruler's confidence; his capacity was deep and restrained.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Xu Jie, through reverence and diligence, won the sovereign's confidence, and his capacity was deep and forbearing.

sentences.zh: 雖任智數，要為不失其正。

translations.literal: Though he employed stratagem, in the essentials he did not lose rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Though he employed stratagem, in the essentials he never lost his rectitude.

sentences.zh: 高拱才略自許，負氣凌人。

translations.literal: Gao Gong prided himself on talent and capacity, and with overbearing spirit looked down on others.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gong prided himself on talent and strategy, and with overbearing spirit looked down on others.

sentences.zh: 及為馮保所逐，柴車即路。

translations.literal: When he was driven out by Feng Bao, he departed by oxcart.
translations.idiomatic: When he was driven out by Feng Bao, he took to the road in an oxcart.

sentences.zh: 傾輒相尋，有自來已。

translations.literal: One downfall after another has followed in succession — this has been so from of old.
translations.idiomatic: One downfall chasing another — such has it always been.

sentences.zh: 張居正通識時變，勇於任事。

translations.literal: Zhang Juzheng thoroughly understood the changes of the times and was bold in undertaking affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng thoroughly understood the changes of the times and was bold in taking on affairs.

sentences.zh: 神宗初政，起衰振隳，不可謂非幹濟才。

translations.literal: In the early government of Emperor Shenzong, he raised what was declining and restored what was ruined; one cannot say he lacked the talent to manage affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the early government of Emperor Shenzong, he raised what was declining and restored what was ruined; one cannot say he was not a man of practical administrative talent.

sentences.zh: 而威柄之操，幾於震主，卒致禍發身後。

translations.literal: Yet in grasping awesome power he nearly overshadowed the ruler, and in the end brought disaster that erupted after his death.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in grasping such awesome power he nearly overshadowed his sovereign, and in the end brought upon himself disaster that erupted after his death.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰「臣罔以寵利居成功」，可弗戒哉！

translations.literal: The Book says, "A minister must not rest in favor and gain upon success" — how could one fail to take warning!
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says, "A minister must not rest in favor and gain upon success" — ought one not take warning from this!
